questions.stem: A new Maine applicant is 17 and has finished studying. Which qualification remains unmet?
options: Age at least 18
Ownership of real estate
Employment by a bank
A law degree
questions.explanation: A Maine applicant must be at least 18.
feedback: Correct. Eighteen is the minimum age.
Property ownership is not required.
Bank employment is not an ordinary qualification.
A law degree is not required.

questions.stem: A New Hampshire resident has a regular workplace in Maine. Which eligibility provision should be considered?
options: Only Maine residents may apply
A Maine place of employment or practice can qualify
A Maine vacation reservation is enough
A friend's Maine address always qualifies
questions.explanation: Maine permits a qualifying place of employment or practice as an alternative to residence.
feedback: The statute includes a work/practice route.
Correct. Verify the actual Maine connection.
A reservation is not employment or practice.
A borrowed address does not establish qualification.

questions.stem: An otherwise eligible applicant cannot read or write English. What statutory requirement matters?
options: Owning a printer
Having an employer sponsor
Ability to read and write English
Using only electronic records
questions.explanation: English reading and writing ability is an applicant qualification.
feedback: Printing equipment does not satisfy this qualification.
Sponsorship does not waive the language requirement.
Correct. The statutory language qualification applies.
Record format does not remove it.

questions.stem: A person without a current Maine commission wants to apply without an examination. What applies?
options: A paid fee waives the examination
Prior work as a witness always waives it
Reading any private blog suffices
The required state or approved examination must be passed
questions.explanation: Section 1923 requires an examination for an applicant who does not hold a current Maine commission.
feedback: Payment does not waive the exam.
Witness experience is not the stated exemption.
Private reading does not establish the required result.
Correct. The statutory examination applies.

questions.stem: A learner wants the official subject coverage before applying. Which material fits §1923?
options: The course covering notarial laws, rules, procedures and ethics
Only a stamp catalog
Only real-estate sales training
Only a wedding script
questions.explanation: The statutory course covers laws, rules, procedures and ethics relevant to notarial acts.
feedback: Correct. These are the prescribed study areas.
A catalog does not cover the required subjects.
Sales training is not the notarial course.
Marriage officiating is a separate role.

questions.stem: A first applicant finds the renewal portal and assumes it is the new-commission filing route. What do the official instructions require?
options: Only a portal profile update
The current new-commission application delivered to the Secretary
A telephone request to a stamp seller
A marriage-officiant surrender form
questions.explanation: New applicants must complete and deliver the most recent commission application.
feedback: A profile update does not submit the required first application.
Correct. Use the current new-commission form.
A seller cannot appoint a Maine notary.
The marriage form is unrelated.

questions.stem: A new applicant asks what application fee the official FAQ states. Which amount is correct?
questions.explanation: The official FAQ identifies the application fee as $50.
feedback: $10 is not the stated fee.
$25 is not the stated fee.
Correct. The fee is $50.
$500 is not the stated fee.

questions.stem: An approved applicant receives a Certificate of Qualification. Who administers the appointment oath?
options: Any customer
The employer's bookkeeper
Any stamp vendor
A Dedimus Justice
questions.explanation: The applicant takes the statutory oath or affirmation before a Dedimus Justice.
feedback: A customer is not authorized merely by being a customer.
Bookkeeping does not establish Dedimus authority.
Selling seals does not establish oath authority.
Correct. A Dedimus Justice administers this oath.

questions.stem: An appointment letter arrives and the applicant schedules the oath 40 days after appointment. What deadline must be met?
options: The oath within 30 calendar days of appointment
The oath at any time in seven years
The oath only at first renewal
The oath after the first notarization
questions.explanation: The official FAQ requires the Dedimus oath within 30 calendar days after appointment.
feedback: Correct. Forty days misses the oath deadline.
The commission term does not replace the qualification deadline.
The first appointment also requires the oath.
The applicant must qualify before acting.

questions.stem: An applicant takes the oath promptly but leaves the completed qualification certificate on a desk. When must it return?
options: Only before retirement
Within 45 calendar days of appointment
Within one year
Only when a client asks
questions.explanation: The completed Certificate of Qualification must return within 45 calendar days of appointment.
feedback: Retirement is unrelated to qualification.
Correct. The separate 45-day return deadline applies.
One year exceeds the deadline.
A client request does not trigger this filing.

questions.stem: An applicant conscientiously objects to oath wording invoking God. What does Maine permit?
options: No appointment under any circumstance
A casual unsigned promise
The statutory affirmation substitutions
A waiver of every qualification step
questions.explanation: Section 1922(3) permits the specified affirmation wording.
feedback: The statute expressly permits affirmation.
The required solemn procedure remains.
Correct. Use the authorized affirmation substitutions.
Affirmation does not remove the qualification process.

questions.stem: A newly qualified Maine notary assumes the term lasts four years because another state does. What term applies?
options: One year
Four years
For life
Seven years
questions.explanation: A Maine notary commission is valid for seven years.
feedback: The ordinary term is not one year.
Another state's term does not govern Maine.
A Maine commission is not lifetime authority.
Correct. The statutory term is seven years.

questions.stem: A Maine notary takes the stamp on a trip to Vermont and wants to notarize there. What territorial rule applies?
options: Maine acts must occur within Maine
Any neighboring state is included
The employer's location controls everywhere
A Maine signer allows acts anywhere
questions.explanation: The official course states Maine notaries may act within Maine and may not act outside it.
feedback: Correct. The notary's physical jurisdiction matters.
Neighboring states are not automatically included.
An employer cannot extend public jurisdiction.
Signer residence does not relocate the notary.

questions.stem: A notary's commission expires in 40 days. Which official service may be used to renew?
options: A private seal order alone
Total Notary Solution online renewal
A county fishing-license service
A wedding-vendor profile
questions.explanation: The official renewal service is available within 45 days before expiration.
feedback: Supplies do not renew authority.
Correct. Forty days falls within the stated pre-expiration window.
That service does not renew commissions.
Wedding services are separate.

questions.stem: A notary expired 60 days ago and asks whether online renewal remains available. What do the official instructions state?
options: No renewal is ever allowed after expiration
Only a 20-day window exists
The service includes expiration within the past 21 to 90 days
The expired notary may act while considering renewal
questions.explanation: The official service allows renewal up to 90 days after expiration, with stated date treatment.
feedback: The service expressly includes a post-expiration window.
The page separately includes days 21 through 90.
Correct. Sixty days is within that listed period.
Renewal availability does not authorize expired acts.

questions.stem: A renewing notary answers an online exam question incorrectly. How does the official service describe progression?
options: The system issues a commission immediately
The notary skips the category
The provider erases the question
A correct response is needed before advancing to the next category
questions.explanation: The renewal instructions say an incorrect response prevents advancement until a correct response is provided.
feedback: An incorrect response does not automatically complete renewal.
The described system does not skip the category.
Erasure is not the stated progression.
Correct. The online service requires a correct response to advance.

questions.stem: A renewal payment is accepted online. What remains in the official process?
options: Print documents, take the Dedimus oath and return the required originals
Nothing because payment alone completes every step
Ask the first customer to issue the commission
Send only a screenshot to the employer
questions.explanation: Online renewal includes printing, the Dedimus oath and mailing the originally signed examination and oath documents.
feedback: Correct. The offline qualification steps remain.
Payment is not the entire renewal process.
A customer cannot issue the commission.
An employer screenshot does not satisfy the return instructions.

questions.stem: Renewal documents did not print at the end of the transaction. What recovery method does the official page identify?
options: Start notarizing without them
Print them from the confirmation email
Ask a stamp vendor to invent them
Discard the renewal
questions.explanation: The instructions say documents may be printed from the confirmation email.
feedback: The missing documents still need completion.
Correct. Use the provided confirmation-email documents.
A vendor cannot invent official forms.
The instructions provide a recovery route.

questions.stem: A notary's address changes and the notary wants to wait until renewal in three years to report it. What does the FAQ require?
options: Only telling the employer
No notice for any address change
Notify the Secretary within 30 calendar days
Post a social-media update only
questions.explanation: Changes to status or submitted information must be reported within 30 calendar days.
feedback: Employer notice does not replace state notice.
The FAQ requires reporting.
Correct. Use the official profile/update process promptly.
A public post does not update the official record.

questions.stem: A commissioned notary changes their name. Which additional document does the FAQ identify?
options: A vehicle title
A passport application for the Secretary
A private customer waiver
The Change of Signature form
questions.explanation: A name change also requires the Change of Signature form submitted to the Secretary.
feedback: A vehicle title is not the specified form.
A passport application does not update the official notary signature.
A waiver does not update the commission record.
Correct. Submit the required signature-change record.

questions.stem: An employer pays for the commission, stamp and journal. Who owns them according to the official course?
options: The notary
The employer automatically
Every coworker jointly
The supplies vendor
questions.explanation: The course states the commission, stamp and journal belong to the notary even if the employer paid.
feedback: Correct. Payment does not transfer ownership.
The course expressly rejects automatic employer ownership.
Coworkers do not share the commission.
The vendor does not retain ownership of the official tools.

questions.stem: A client asks a notary to solemnize a wedding solely under the notary commission. What changed on July 1, 2023?
options: Every notary became a judge
Marriage officiating is a separate licensed office
The commission became a marriage certificate
No oath is ever needed again
questions.explanation: The FAQ explains that notary marriage authority was repealed and a separate Marriage Officiant office created.
feedback: Notaries did not become judges.
Correct. Verify separate marriage-officiant authority.
The commission is not a marriage certificate.
Commission qualification requirements continue.

questions.stem: An applicant assumes a commission gives all immunities and benefits of Maine public employees. What does §1922(5) state?
options: Every public-employee benefit applies
All liability disappears
The commission confers no such statutory immunity or benefit
The bond company decides public benefits
questions.explanation: The commission authorizes acts and does not confer public-official or employee immunities or benefits.
feedback: The statute expressly limits this assumption.
A commission does not erase liability.
Correct. The specific no-immunity-or-benefit provision applies.
A surety does not grant public benefits.

questions.stem: A client asks whether every Maine notarial officer must also hold a Secretary-issued notary commission. Which person may have statutory authority independently?
options: Any receptionist
Any loan officer
Any real-estate agent
A duly admitted attorney eligible to practice in Maine courts
questions.explanation: Section 1910 includes qualifying attorneys and specified court officers among notarial officers.
feedback: Reception work alone supplies no such authority.
Loan employment alone is insufficient.
A real-estate license alone is insufficient.
Correct. The statute expressly includes qualifying attorneys.

questions.stem: A first applicant relies on an old form found in an office drawer. What do current instructions direct?
options: Use the most recent application form
Use any historical form indefinitely
Replace it with a journal page
Submit only a stamp impression
questions.explanation: New applicants must complete and deliver the most recent application.
feedback: Correct. Obtain the current official form.
Historical forms may omit current requirements.
A journal page is not the application.
A stamp impression does not supply an application.

questions.stem: An applicant asks this practice pack to guarantee the current first-examination question count. What is supported by verified sources?
options: Exactly 50 questions in every first exam
The examination requirement is verified but current count and time remain unverified
Exactly five questions in every first exam
No examination is required
questions.explanation: The statute verifies the examination and course requirement. Current first-exam count, duration and percentage were not verified.
feedback: That count was not verified for Maine.
Correct. Preserve the documented specification limits.
That count was not verified for Maine.
The statute requires the examination.

questions.stem: A notary updates a phone number through the official profile service. What fee does the resources page state for commission-information updates?
options: $50 for every update
No fee
A fee per client in the journal
questions.explanation: The official resources page states there is no fee to update commission information.
feedback: The renewal fee is a different charge.
This is not the stated update fee.
Correct. The page identifies no update fee.
Client volume does not set the update charge.

questions.stem: A nonresident applicant has neither Maine residence nor a Maine place of employment or practice. What is missing?
options: A particular stamp shape
A Maine customer testimonial
An expensive training package
The statutory Maine residence/work/practice connection
questions.explanation: Section 1922 requires residence or a qualifying employment/practice location in Maine.
feedback: Stamp shape does not establish eligibility.
A testimonial does not create the statutory connection.
Buying training does not establish the connection.
Correct. One of the stated Maine connections is required.

questions.stem: A newly appointed applicant misses both qualification deadlines and receives a failure-to-qualify notice. What remedy period does the FAQ identify?
options: Request reappointment within 90 calendar days after that notice
Act for 90 days without qualifying
Ignore the notice for seven years
Ask any client to reinstate the commission
questions.explanation: The FAQ allows 90 calendar days from the failure notice to request reappointment.
feedback: Correct. The period concerns requesting reappointment.
It does not grant unqualified practice authority.
The commission term does not cancel qualification requirements.
A client cannot reinstate the appointment.

questions.stem: A person paid the renewal fee after the old commission expired and wants to resume before completing qualification. What should govern?
options: A receipt alone creates immediate authority
Complete the required qualification and effective commission process before acting
The old expiration date disappears automatically
An employer can extend the old term
questions.explanation: Renewal payment does not eliminate the oath and required original-document return steps.
feedback: The process includes additional required steps.
Correct. Complete the state qualification process.
Expiration does not disappear through payment alone.
An employer cannot extend public authority.

questions.stem: A Maine notary has known a customer through years of dealings. What standard supports personal knowledge?
options: The customer's fame online
Reasonable certainty from sufficient personal dealings
A matching surname alone
A paid service fee
questions.explanation: Section 1907 requires dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of the claimed identity.
feedback: Online fame alone is not the stated relationship.
Correct. Sufficient dealings support personal knowledge.
A name match does not establish personal knowledge.
Payment does not identify the signer.

questions.stem: An unknown signer offers a government identification form other than a passport, driver's license or nondriver card. What feature can satisfy the alternative statutory category?
options: Only a bank balance
Only the employer's logo
A signature or photograph, with the credential satisfactory to the officer
Only a typed promise
questions.explanation: The alternative government-ID category requires a signature or photograph and satisfaction of the officer.
feedback: A balance does not meet the credential category.
An employer logo is not the statutory feature.
Correct. The statute uses signature or photograph.
A typed promise is not qualifying government identification.

questions.stem: A witness unknown to the notary personally appears, is identified by a driver's license and solemnly verifies the principal's identity. What does Maine permit?
options: Only personally known witnesses ever qualify
Witnesses never assist identity
Only an employer may witness
The qualifying identified credible-witness route
questions.explanation: The credible witness may be known to the officer or identified through the specified credentials.
feedback: Maine includes a credential-identified witness option.
The statute expressly permits credible witnesses.
The method is not limited to employers.
Correct. The statutory witness identity route is available.

questions.stem: A witness identifies a signer in casual conversation but refuses an oath or affirmation. What is missing?
options: The required sworn or affirmed verification
The witness's property ownership
The notary's employer approval
A second application fee
questions.explanation: The credible-witness method requires verification on oath or affirmation.
feedback: Correct. An unsworn introduction is insufficient.
Property ownership does not supply the verification.
Employer approval does not administer an oath.
Application fees are unrelated.

questions.stem: A credential leaves the notary uncertain about identity. What additional authority does §1907 provide?
options: An obligation to accept it immediately
The ability to require additional information or credentials
Authority to invent a new identity
A requirement to borrow the signer's password
questions.explanation: The officer may require additional information or credentials necessary to assure identity.
feedback: The statute permits further assurance.
Correct. Additional identity evidence may be requested.
The notary must determine actual identity.
Private account access is not the stated statutory method.

questions.stem: A courier brings an absent customer's signed document and ID. What requirement remains?
options: Only a larger fee
Only a stamp purchase
The person's lawful personal appearance
Only the courier's business card
questions.explanation: The official course requires the signer to appear. A courier's papers do not create that appearance.
feedback: Payment cannot replace appearance.
Supplies cannot replace the person.
Correct. Use a lawful appearance procedure.
The courier's card identifies a different person.

questions.stem: A person's name is typed on a contract. Does that alone identify the arriving signer?
options: Yes, typed names are conclusive
Yes, if the contract is long
Yes, if a company prepared it
No, use personal knowledge or satisfactory statutory evidence
questions.explanation: The notary must identify the actual appearing individual under §1907.
feedback: Typed text does not establish who appeared.
Length does not identify a person.
Company preparation does not replace identity evidence.
Correct. Apply an authorized identity route.

questions.stem: A principal cannot physically sign due to disability and directs an assistant. Who may sign under §1909?
options: An individual other than the notarial officer at the principal's direction
Only the notary personally
Any person without the principal's direction
Only the document recipient
questions.explanation: The statute permits a directed individual other than the notarial officer to sign.
feedback: Correct. The principal's direction and third-person signer are required.
The statute excludes the notarial officer as directed signer.
Direction is part of the statutory procedure.
The recipient is not the sole permitted category.

questions.stem: A directed third-person signature is used because of disability. What must the officer insert?
options: Only a fee amount
Words identifying who affixed the signature and at whose direction
Only the assistant's telephone number
A statement that no one signed
questions.explanation: Section 1909 requires the prescribed or similar directed-signature statement.
feedback: The fee does not describe the execution.
Correct. Identify both the signer and directing principal.
A phone number does not supply the required statement.
The statement must describe what occurred.

questions.stem: A signer seems unable to understand the transaction's consequences. What statutory response is available?
options: Proceed if the ID is current
Let a relative waive all concerns
Refuse if not satisfied about competence or capacity
Ask the vendor to decide legal capacity
questions.explanation: Section 1908 permits refusal when the officer is not satisfied of competence or capacity.
feedback: Identity does not resolve capacity.
A relative's waiver does not compel the act.
Correct. The statute expressly permits refusal on this basis.
The officer must exercise the required judgment.

questions.stem: A companion threatens a signer who appears reluctant. Which statutory issue should the notary assess?
options: The companion's clothing
The document's page count
The fee receipt color
Whether the signature is knowingly and voluntarily made
questions.explanation: Section 1908 permits refusal when the officer is not satisfied of knowing, voluntary execution.
feedback: Clothing does not resolve voluntariness.
Page count does not establish free choice.
Receipt color is irrelevant.
Correct. Evaluate the signer's knowing and voluntary act.

questions.stem: An old lease signature is presented for acknowledgment by the now-appearing identified signer. What does the course permit?
options: Acknowledgment of the earlier signature
No acknowledgment of any earlier signature
Only a new commission application
An absent-person acknowledgment by mail
questions.explanation: The acknowledgment course permits signing before or during notarization while requiring appearance.
feedback: Correct. The signer still makes the acknowledgment.
The course expressly permits a prior signature.
This is a notarial act, not an application.
A prior signature does not remove appearance.

questions.stem: An affidavit already bears a signature but requests verification upon oath. What does the course direct?
options: Use the old signature with no ceremony
Have the signer sign again before the officer and administer oath or affirmation
Treat the signature as a witness's
Only photograph the affidavit
questions.explanation: The verification procedure calls for signing in the officer's presence, including signing again if already signed.
feedback: The sworn-signing procedure remains necessary.
Correct. Follow the actual verification steps.
Reclassifying the signature does not perform the act.
A photograph does not administer a verification.

questions.stem: A signer prefers a nonreligious solemn pledge for a verification. Which form is available?
options: Only an oath invoking God
A silent nod with no declaration
An affirmation on personal honor
An automatic waiver of truth
questions.explanation: The official course describes affirmation as a spoken pledge on personal honor.
feedback: The signer may choose affirmation.
The required solemn declaration still occurs.
Correct. Affirmation is authorized.
Affirmation does not waive truthfulness.

questions.stem: A signature-witnessing page was signed before the appointment. What should the course procedure require?
options: Only an oral acknowledgment in every case
Only a seal on the old signature
Only an email from the employer
Signing again in the officer's presence
questions.explanation: The witnessing course instructs that an already signed record must be signed again before the officer.
feedback: The requested witnessed signing has its own procedure.
A seal does not create an observed event.
An email cannot witness the actual signing.
Correct. The signature must be witnessed.

questions.stem: A signature-witnessing act is properly performed. Does the official course require a verbal oath for that form?
options: No verbal ceremony is necessary for witnessing or attesting a signature
A religious oath is always mandatory
An oath replaces the signature
Only an employer's oath is needed
questions.explanation: The course states no verbal ceremony is necessary for witnessing or attesting a signature.
feedback: Correct. The identified person must still sign before the officer.
The course does not require an oath for this form.
An oath does not replace the signing.
Employer participation does not perform the signer's act.

questions.stem: A corporate agent acknowledges a record. What representative declaration does the course describe?
options: That the notary owns the company
Proper authority and execution as the identified entity's act
That all corporate debts are guaranteed
That identification is waived
questions.explanation: Representative acknowledgment includes proper authority and signing as the act of the identified represented entity.
feedback: The notary's ownership is unrelated.
Correct. The declaration addresses authority and representative execution.
The act does not guarantee debts.
The representative still must be identified.

questions.stem: A document lacks a notarial certificate and the client asks the notary to select a legal act for them. What does the FAQ direct?
options: Select any act with the shortest form
Stamp without a certificate
Have the signer choose, using examples or recipient guidance if needed
Use an expired commission certificate
questions.explanation: The FAQ makes certificate selection the signer's decision and allows examples or recipient consultation.
feedback: Convenience does not select the customer's legal act.
Every act requires a certificate.
Correct. The signer decides which certificate to affix.
A commission certificate is not the transaction's notarial certificate.

questions.stem: A completed paper certificate omits the notarial officer's office title. What should be added?
options: Only the employer's slogan
Only the signer's job
Only a stamp vendor's name
The title of the notarial office
questions.explanation: The certificate must contain the notarial officer's title.
feedback: A slogan does not identify public office.
The signer's job is a different fact.
The vendor's name does not identify the officer's title.
Correct. Include the officer's title.

questions.stem: A Maine notary signs the certificate using a style different from the signature on file. What does §1916 require?
options: Signing in the same manner as on file with the Secretary
Any customer-selected signature
Only the employer's initials
No signature if a stamp is used
questions.explanation: A notary public signs the certificate in the same manner as on file with the Secretary.
feedback: Correct. Use the official filed signature manner.
A customer cannot choose the notary's signature.
Employer initials do not execute the notary's certificate.
A stamp does not remove the signature requirement.

questions.stem: A notary performs an act in York County for a record drafted in Portland. Which jurisdiction belongs in the certificate?
options: The drafting location automatically
The jurisdiction of the performed notarial act
The recipient's headquarters
The signer's birthplace
questions.explanation: The certificate identifies the jurisdiction in which the notarial act is performed.
feedback: Drafting does not determine the act's location.
Correct. Use the actual act jurisdiction.
The recipient's location does not set the venue.
Birthplace does not locate the act.

questions.stem: A notary's certificate gives the act date and name but omits commission expiration. What applies?
options: Expiration is never included
A client may waive it
A notary public's certificate must indicate commission expiration
Only a journal number is needed
questions.explanation: Section 1916 requires the notary public's commission expiration date in the certificate.
feedback: The statute expressly requires it.
Client preference does not remove the field.
Correct. Include the commission expiration date.
A journal number does not replace the required certificate information.

questions.stem: A paper certificate has the notary's signature but no legibly printed or typed name. What is missing?
options: The notary's middle-school record
A customer testimonial
The application fee
The legibly printed or typed officer name
questions.explanation: Section 1916(1)(F) requires a legible printed or typed name.
feedback: School history is unrelated.
A testimonial does not identify the official in the required way.
A fee does not supply certificate content.
Correct. The legible name is a required field.

questions.stem: A customer wants a signed certificate now and promises to appear tomorrow. When may the officer sign it?
options: After the actual notarial act has been performed
Whenever the customer prepays
Before identification if the customer is busy
At any time during the commission
questions.explanation: The officer may not sign or logically associate a certificate until the act has been performed.
feedback: Correct. The act precedes certificate execution.
Payment cannot authorize advance certification.
Identification and the ceremony cannot be deferred.
Current commissioning does not authorize certificates for unperformed acts.

questions.stem: A separate paper certificate is prepared for a document. What connection is required?
options: No connection to the document
It must be part of or securely attached to the record
Only a verbal promise to attach later
Keep it with unrelated office files
questions.explanation: A tangible-record certificate must be part of or securely attached to that record.
feedback: The statute requires association with the record.
Correct. Preserve the document-certificate connection.
A promise does not attach the certificate.
Unrelated storage does not attach it.

questions.stem: A notary applies only a stamp to an in-person paper document and leaves no certificate. What requirement was missed?
options: A mandatory electronic platform for every paper act
A wedding license
A certificate evidencing the act
A second passport
questions.explanation: Every notarial act must be evidenced by the required certificate.
feedback: Ordinary in-person paper acts do not require an electronic platform.
A wedding license is unrelated.
Correct. A stamp alone is not the certificate.
An additional passport does not supply the certificate.

questions.stem: For an ordinary in-person paper act, what does the official course say about using a stamp?
options: Always prohibited
Always required by the journal statute
It replaces the certificate
Optional under this rule, with use strongly suggested unless prohibited
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes optional in-person paper stamping from required electronic or remote stamping.
feedback: The course recommends use unless prohibited.
The journal statute does not impose this universal stamp rule.
A stamp does not replace the certificate.
Correct. Preserve the stated scope and recommendation.

questions.stem: A custom Maine stamp cannot be reproduced together with the document. Which statutory requirement fails?
options: The copied-together reproducibility requirement
A mandatory blue border
A required employer logo
A requirement to use invisible ink
questions.explanation: The official stamp must be capable of being copied with the associated record.
feedback: Correct. Reproducibility is required.
The statute does not impose that border color.
An employer logo is not required.
Invisible ink would not satisfy reproducibility.

questions.stem: A notary asks whether the act's certificate can be dated from the contract's drafting day. What date belongs?
options: The drafting date automatically
The date of the actual performed notarial act
The date the stamp was bought
The customer's birthday
questions.explanation: The certificate is executed contemporaneously and dated by the officer to evidence the act.
feedback: Drafting does not establish the notarial date.
Correct. Record the actual act date.
A supply purchase does not date the act.
A birthday is unrelated.

questions.stem: A notary witnesses a signature but signs a certificate stating an oath was administered. What should be corrected?
options: Only the fee receipt
Only the envelope
The certificate must accurately describe the performed act
Nothing because all acts are identical
questions.explanation: A sufficient certificate sets forth actions that satisfy the actual act.
feedback: A receipt does not correct an inaccurate certificate.
An envelope is unrelated.
Correct. Certificate facts must match the ceremony.
The statutes distinguish the acts.

questions.stem: A friend introduces a stranger as an old classmate of the friend. The notary has no dealings with the stranger. What does that establish?
options: Automatic personal knowledge by the notary
A complete sworn witness procedure
A qualifying passport
No sufficient identity method by itself
questions.explanation: The introduction alone is neither the notary's personal knowledge nor a sworn credible-witness verification.
feedback: Another person's acquaintance is not the officer's dealings.
No oath or affirmation occurred.
An introduction is not a passport.
Correct. Establish a statutory identity basis.

questions.stem: A signer whose disability prevents writing directs another individual to sign. Must the notary truthfully describe that method?
options: Yes, insert the required directed-signature wording or similar words
No, hide the assistance
No, call it the notary's own signature
Only if the helper charges a fee
questions.explanation: Section 1909 requires the stated or similar notation identifying the directed signature.
feedback: Correct. The execution method must be recorded as required.
Concealment omits the required statement.
The assistant's signature is not the notary's signature.
The notation does not depend on a fee.

questions.stem: A notary is asked to refuse solely because a document's language is unfamiliar. What does the official course say?
options: Every foreign-language document must be rejected
That fact alone is not a reason the course says to refuse
The notary must translate every word personally
The notary may ignore identity and certificate requirements
questions.explanation: The course lists an unfamiliar document language among reasons not to refuse by itself.
feedback: The course does not impose a categorical rejection.
Correct. The actual act and other requirements still need to be satisfied.
The course does not require personal translation of every word.
Normal identity and certificate requirements remain.

questions.stem: A customer presents an original private employment agreement and asks for a certified copy. What must the officer determine?
options: The agreement will never be disputed
The employer is profitable
The copy is a full, true and accurate reproduction
The customer is a lawyer
questions.explanation: Copy certification requires determining that the copy fully and accurately reproduces the record.
feedback: Future disputes are outside the certification.
Profitability is unrelated.
Correct. The statutory determination concerns the copy.
Lawyer status is not required for the customer.

questions.stem: A customer asks a Maine notary to certify a photocopy of a birth certificate. What does the official course direct?
options: Certify every copy if a fee is paid
Certify only the seal image
Erase the record's title first
Do not make certified copies of vital records
questions.explanation: The course excludes vital-record copy certification by the notary.
feedback: Payment does not authorize the excluded certification.
Copying a seal does not change the record category.
Altering a title does not change the underlying record.
Correct. Use the authorized vital-record source.

questions.stem: A publicly recorded deed is available as a certified copy from the official custodian. What should the notary do?
options: Direct the requester to the official certified-copy source
Certify the public record as a private contract
Remove the recording information
Ask the requester to rename the deed
questions.explanation: The course excludes public records and publicly recorded documents available from an official certified-copy source.
feedback: Correct. The official source supplies the certified public record.
Renaming the category does not authorize the act.
Removing information does not make the act lawful.
A new label cannot change the record's nature.

questions.stem: A record states on its face that copying it is illegal. What does the course say about notarial copy certification?
options: It is always mandatory
Do not certify a copy of that record
The notary's stamp overrides the restriction
A customer waiver overrides it
questions.explanation: The course says an officer may not certify a copy of a record bearing that facial prohibition.
feedback: The course identifies a restriction.
Correct. The facial prohibition must be respected.
A stamp does not override the restriction.
A waiver does not create authority.

questions.stem: A private document has six pages, but the copy omits an exhibit page. Can the notary certify it as a full reproduction?
options: Yes, if the signature page is included
Yes, if the missing page seems unimportant
No, the missing material defeats the full-copy determination
Only if the fee is reduced
questions.explanation: A full, true and accurate copy must reproduce the complete record being certified.
feedback: A signature page alone is not the full record.
The notary cannot omit material under a full-copy statement.
Correct. Resolve the incomplete reproduction before certification.
A fee reduction cannot cure the missing page.

questions.stem: A reproduction crops out handwritten terms from the original private record. What must occur before certification as a full accurate copy?
options: The customer must initial the crop
The notary may ignore handwriting
The recipient must promise not to complain
Obtain a full accurate reproduction including the omitted terms
questions.explanation: The officer must determine that the reproduction is full, true and accurate.
feedback: Initials do not make the crop complete.
Handwritten content is part of the presented record.
A promise does not cure inaccuracy.
Correct. The copy must reproduce the record fully.

questions.stem: A notary certifies an eligible copy and the customer asks whether this guarantees the original is authentic. What does the course explain?
options: The certification concerns accurate copying and does not guarantee the original's authenticity
It guarantees every signature on the original
It proves every promise is enforceable
It constitutes a court judgment
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes copy accuracy from the original record's authenticity, contents and effects.
feedback: Correct. The officer certifies the reproduction.
The act does not authenticate every original signature.
It does not guarantee legal effects.
A notarial certificate is not a court judgment.

questions.stem: A customer asks whether a certified copy proves the truth of every statement in the source record. What is accurate?
options: Every copied statement becomes proven
The copy act does not guarantee the record's contents
Only statements printed in black become true
The recipient decides whether the notary knew the facts
questions.explanation: The copy act addresses reproduction accuracy and does not guarantee contents.
feedback: Accurate reproduction does not prove factual truth.
Correct. The source's factual truth is a different question.
Ink color does not establish truth.
Recipient preference does not change the act's scope.

questions.stem: A copy certificate states that the notary made the photocopy, but the notary only compared a customer-supplied copy with the original. What should be used?
options: The inaccurate made-by-me statement
No certificate
A truthful comparison certificate matching the actual procedure
A blank certificate for the recipient
questions.explanation: The course provides distinct certificate language for a made copy and a carefully compared copy.
feedback: The certificate must not misstate the method.
Copy certification still requires a certificate.
Correct. Use the form that truthfully describes the comparison.
Blank certification is not a substitute.

questions.stem: A stranger presents an original eligible private record for copying. What is the first step in the course's copy procedure?
options: Guarantee the contents
Administer an automatic marriage oath
Check the notary's tax return
Verify the custodian's identity if not personally known
questions.explanation: The course's copy procedure starts with identifying the record custodian if not personally known.
feedback: The act does not guarantee contents.
A marriage oath is unrelated.
The notary's tax records are irrelevant.
Correct. Follow the custodian identification step.

questions.stem: The requester supplies only a photocopy and asks the notary to state it was compared with the original. What evidence is missing?
options: The original for the claimed comparison
The customer's business logo
A stamp invoice
A list of coworkers
questions.explanation: A truthful comparison statement requires the actual original presented for comparison.
feedback: Correct. The notary cannot certify an unperformed comparison.
A logo does not supply the original.
An invoice does not supply the source record.
Coworker names do not enable comparison.

questions.stem: An officer personally makes an accurate photocopy of an eligible original private instrument. What should follow?
options: Issue only an oral assurance
Complete, sign and securely attach the copy certificate
Send the original to a private advertiser
Skip the certificate because the officer used the copier
questions.explanation: The copy procedure requires completion and secure attachment of the notarial certificate.
feedback: An oral assurance does not supply the certificate.
Correct. Complete the documented copy act.
Advertising disclosure is unrelated to certification.
Making the copy does not eliminate certification.

questions.stem: A copy certificate is stapled to the photocopy so removal leaves evidence. How does this fit the course?
options: The course requires keeping it loose
The staple replaces the officer's signature
It follows the described secure attachment method
It makes an ineligible vital record eligible
questions.explanation: The course specifically describes stapling the signed certificate to the photocopy to leave tampering evidence.
feedback: The course calls for secure attachment.
The officer must still sign.
Correct. The described staple supports the required connection.
Attachment does not change record eligibility.

questions.stem: A customer asks the notary to certify a printed copy of an electronic record. What authority does Maine provide?
options: No officer can ever certify any printout
Only a private vendor may certify it
The act automatically proves legal validity
The officer may certify a tangible copy as an accurate copy of the electronic record
questions.explanation: Section 1904(2) expressly authorizes certification of an accurate tangible copy of an electronic record.
feedback: The statute expressly provides authority.
Authority is given to the notarial officer.
Accuracy does not guarantee legal validity.
Correct. The statute authorizes the accurate-copy certification.

questions.stem: A printed electronic record differs from the electronic source because a table is missing. What must the officer do?
options: Resolve the discrepancy before certifying accuracy
Certify because both show the same title
Ignore tables as formatting
Use a larger stamp
questions.explanation: Certification of the tangible copy requires actual accuracy to the electronic source.
feedback: Correct. The missing table defeats the proposed accuracy statement.
A title match does not establish completeness.
Substantive tables cannot simply be disregarded.
Stamp size does not cure missing content.

questions.stem: A notary watches a clerk make the copy of an eligible original private record. Which course method can support certification?
options: Only trusting the clerk's later email
Witnessing the making of the photocopy and completing the required verification
Only stamping the original
Only charging a copying fee
questions.explanation: The course permits personally making the copy or witnessing its making, with the full accurate-copy determination.
feedback: Later assurance alone is not the observed procedure.
Correct. Witnessed copying is described in the course.
Stamping the original does not certify the copy.
Payment does not establish accuracy.

questions.stem: A scanned copy is unreadable in several paragraphs. May it be certified as the full true reproduction of the readable original?
options: Yes, if the file name matches
Yes, if the scanner is new
No, the officer must establish an accurate reproduction
Yes, if the customer agrees to the blur
questions.explanation: The officer must determine that the copy accurately reproduces the original record.
feedback: A filename does not reproduce missing readable content.
Equipment age does not cure unreadability.
Correct. Obtain a reproduction that supports the certification.
Consent does not make unreadable content accurate.

questions.stem: A requester asks the notary to remove an unfavorable paragraph from a private original and certify the result as complete. What applies?
options: The requester may define every altered copy as exact
A lower fee permits the omission
A stamp can authenticate any edit
The proposed full-copy certification would be false
questions.explanation: A full, true and accurate reproduction cannot deliberately omit source content.
feedback: The source determines what a full copy contains.
Fees do not authorize false certification.
A stamp does not make an altered copy exact.
Correct. Do not certify the edited record as the complete source.

questions.stem: An eligible private-record copy is accurate, but the certificate states a comparison date that never occurred. What should happen?
options: Use truthful certificate facts for the actual act
Keep the date if the customer requests it
Delete the officer's name instead
Assume copy accuracy cures all false certificate details
questions.explanation: The certificate is signed and dated for the actual performed notarial act.
feedback: Correct. Copy accuracy does not excuse false certificate facts.
A customer cannot require false dating.
Deleting the name would create another defect.
Each required certificate fact must be accurate.

questions.stem: A customer wants a notarial copy of a death certificate available from the vital-record authority. Which source should supply the certified record?
options: The notary's employer
The authorized vital-record custodian
A social-media contact
Any person with a photocopier
questions.explanation: The course excludes notarial certification of vital records.
feedback: Employment does not create vital-record certification authority.
Correct. Use the official record source.
An online contact does not confer authority.
Equipment ownership does not authorize certification.

questions.stem: A customer thinks copy certification is an oath that the source document's promises will be fulfilled. What does the course describe?
options: A financial guarantee
A judicial finding
The officer's statement of accurate reproduction
An automatic acknowledgment of every signature
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes copy certification from taking an oath or acknowledgment.
feedback: The act does not guarantee performance.
The notary is not adjudicating the instrument.
Correct. The officer certifies the copy's accuracy.
The act does not automatically acknowledge source signatures.

questions.stem: A document recipient asks for an apostille after receiving a notarized copy. Who issues the authority certification described in the course?
options: The document custodian
The notary's employer
The copy-machine manufacturer
The Secretary of State
questions.explanation: The course describes apostilles and authentications as Secretary-issued certifications of official authority.
feedback: The custodian does not issue the described state certification.
Employer status does not confer apostille authority.
The manufacturer does not authenticate public authority.
Correct. The Secretary issues the authority certification.

questions.stem: A notary performs an in-person paper copy certification and keeps a journal voluntarily. How should the course's journal step be described?
options: Strongly recommended for this paper act, while electronic and remote journals are mandatory
Always forbidden
A substitute for the copy certificate
A guarantee of the original's contents
questions.explanation: The copy procedure recommends recording the act, while the journal statute distinguishes paper from electronic/remote acts.
feedback: Correct. Preserve the duty/recommendation distinction.
Voluntary paper journals are permitted.
The journal does not replace the certificate.
A journal entry does not guarantee source contents.

questions.stem: A copier reproduces only the front of a two-sided original containing terms on both sides. What is the proper response?
options: Certify the front as the entire original
Reproduce and verify all content before certifying a full copy
Ask the client to ignore the back
Omit the source description
questions.explanation: A full accurate reproduction must include the source content covered by the certificate.
feedback: The front alone is not the entire two-sided record.
Correct. Complete the reproduction and verification.
Ignoring content does not satisfy accuracy.
Omitting a description does not cure incompleteness.

questions.stem: A notary is offered an accurate copy of an ineligible public record. Which issue should be resolved first?
options: Only whether the copy is attractive
Only whether the customer pays
Whether the record is eligible for notarial copy certification
Only whether the copy uses color
questions.explanation: Accuracy alone does not remove the course's public- and vital-record exclusions.
feedback: Appearance does not establish authority.
Payment does not make an excluded record eligible.
Correct. Eligibility and accuracy are both necessary.
Color does not determine public-record eligibility.

questions.stem: A Maine notary performs only traditional in-person paper acts. What does §1920 require about keeping a journal for those acts?
options: A separate journal for every client
No journal may ever be used
Only a video recording
A journal is permitted, while the Secretary strongly recommends it
questions.explanation: Tangible in-person journal keeping is optional under the statute and strongly recommended by the official guidance.
feedback: Multiple client-specific journals conflict with the one-journal tangible rule.
Voluntary journaling is permitted.
A video does not express this paper journal rule.
Correct. Preserve the statutory scope and recommendation.

questions.stem: A notary begins approved in-person electronic notarizations but keeps no journal because the signer is in the room. What applies?
options: A journal is mandatory for electronic acts
Only remote location triggers a journal
Electronic records are never journaled
The employer can waive the journal
questions.explanation: All electronic and remote notarizations require a journal.
feedback: Correct. Electronic format triggers the duty even with in-person appearance.
The statute also includes electronic acts.
The statute expressly requires recording them.
An employer cannot waive the statutory duty.

questions.stem: A remote paper act is performed and the notary assumes paper means no journal is required. What controls?
options: Paper always removes the journal duty
Remote notarization requires a journal
Only the signer's request matters
Only charged acts require entries
questions.explanation: The statute requires journals for all remote notarizations.
feedback: Remote performance is independently covered.
Correct. The remote journal duty applies.
A request does not determine the statutory duty.
The duty does not depend on charging.

questions.stem: A journal's final act occurred three years ago and the notary retires. What retention period applies?
options: Only until retirement
Five years from purchasing the journal
Ten years after the last act chronicled
Only until the stamp is replaced
questions.explanation: Retain the journal for ten years after the performance of its last recorded act.
feedback: Retirement does not end retention.
The anchor is the last act, not purchase.
Correct. The statutory ten-year period applies.
Stamp replacement does not end retention.

questions.stem: A paper notary wants one active journal at each of three offices for tangible acts. What statutory limit applies?
options: Unlimited tangible journals
Exactly three journals
One journal per customer
Only one journal at a time for tangible-record acts

feedback: The statute imposes a limit.
Office count does not alter that limit.
Customer-specific journals do not satisfy the stated arrangement.
Correct. The tangible-record rule is one active journal.

questions.stem: A notary uses two approved electronic systems and asks whether more than one electronic-record journal may be maintained. What does §1920 permit?
options: One or more journals for electronic-record acts
No electronic journals
Only paper journals
Only one lifetime journal of any type
questions.explanation: The statute allows one or more journals for acts concerning electronic records.
feedback: Correct. The electronic-record rule permits multiple journals.
Electronic journals are expressly allowed.
The statute allows electronic formats.
The statute does not impose a single lifetime volume.

questions.stem: A notary proposes a paper journal made of loose sheets in a folder. What physical format is required?
options: Any unbound collection
A permanent bound register with numbered pages
Only a spreadsheet printout with no binding
Only a decorative cover
questions.explanation: A tangible journal must be a permanent bound register with numbered pages.
feedback: Loose pages do not meet the stated format.
Correct. Binding and numbered pages are required.
Unbound printouts do not provide the required format.
A cover alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: An electronic journal allows silent editing of completed entries. What format does Maine require?
options: Any editable note file
Only an email draft
A permanent tamper-evident electronic format
Only a public social-media post
questions.explanation: The electronic journal must be permanent and tamper-evident under applicable rules.
feedback: An unrestricted note file lacks required integrity.
An email draft is not necessarily compliant.
Correct. The electronic format must reveal tampering.
A public post does not meet the journal safeguards.

questions.stem: A notary postpones required entries until the end of the month. When must an entry be made?
options: At retirement
At the next renewal
Only after a complaint
Contemporaneously with the act
questions.explanation: Journal entries must be made contemporaneously with performance.
feedback: Retirement is too late.
Renewal is too late.
A complaint does not trigger the original entry duty.
Correct. Record the act when it occurs.

questions.stem: A required journal entry records the date but omits the time. What must be added?
options: The time of the act
The signer's bank balance
The notary's tax number
The employer's profit
questions.explanation: The entry must contain both date and time.
feedback: Correct. Time is a required field.
A balance is unrelated.
The notary's tax number is not the missing field.

options: The customer's political views
A description of the record and type of notarial act
The stamp vendor's mailing list
The notary's commuting route
questions.explanation: The journal includes the record description, if any, and act type.
feedback: Political views do not describe the required transaction.
Correct. Identify both record and act type.
A vendor list is unrelated.
A route is unrelated.

questions.stem: A required entry identifies a customer only by initials. What does §1920 specify?
options: Initials always suffice
Only an anonymous client number
The individual's full name and address
Only the employer's name
questions.explanation: The entry must contain each individual's full name and address.
feedback: Initials do not provide the full name.
A number does not replace name and address.

The employer's identity does not identify the customer.

options: A made-up passport number
Only a signature image
Only the fee
A statement that identity was based on personal knowledge

feedback: Do not invent evidence.
A signature image does not state the identity method.
The fee is a different field.
Correct. Record the actual personal-knowledge basis.

questions.stem: A required act uses documentary evidence. What credential details does the journal statute specify?
options: Brief method/credential description including issuance and expiration dates
Only the credential's color
Only the signer's occupation
No identification details
questions.explanation: Record the method and credential description with issuance and expiration dates.
feedback: Correct. These are the specified details.
Color alone omits required information.
Occupation does not describe the credential.
The statute requires the identification record.

questions.stem: A notary charges a fee for a remote act but omits it from the journal. What is required?
options: Only a private oral quote
The fee, if any, in the entry
Only a bank transfer number
Only the vendor's advertisement

feedback: A quote does not replace the journal field.
Correct. Record the charged notarial fee.
A transaction number does not state the fee.
An advertisement does not record this act.

questions.stem: A journal is stolen from a vehicle. What notice does Maine require?
options: Wait until renewal
No notice if it was optional
Promptly notify the Secretary upon discovery
Only tell a customer next year
questions.explanation: The officer must promptly notify the Secretary after discovering a lost or stolen journal.
feedback: The statute calls for prompt notice.
The loss provision applies to the officer's journal.
Correct. Notify the Secretary promptly.
A later customer conversation does not satisfy state notice.

questions.stem: A notary resigns and wants to throw away the journal. What does §1920 require?
options: Immediate destruction
Automatic transfer to the employer
Posting every entry online
Retain it for the required period and tell the Secretary its location
questions.explanation: Resignation requires retention under the ten-year rule and notice of the journal's location.
feedback: Resignation does not authorize destruction.
The statute does not make the employer the automatic recipient.
Public posting does not satisfy secure retention.

questions.stem: A former notary cannot retain the journal personally. What alternative does §1920 provide?
options: Transmit it to the Secretary or an approved repository
Give it to any customer
Leave it at a public library table
Sell it with the office furniture
questions.explanation: The statute permits transmission to the Secretary or a repository approved by the Secretary.
feedback: Correct. Use an authorized recipient.
A random customer is not the statutory repository.
Abandonment does not preserve custody.
A furniture sale is not authorized disposition.

questions.stem: A notary dies and a representative knowingly holds the journal. What must the representative do?
options: Discard it with household papers
Transmit it to the Secretary or an approved repository
Give every entry to a marketing company
Keep it secretly without regard to the statute
questions.explanation: The personal representative, guardian or knowing possessor has the stated transmission duty.
feedback: The statute requires preservation and transmission.
Correct. Use one of the statutory recipients.
Marketing disclosure is not the required disposition.
Possession carries the statutory duty.

questions.stem: A commission is suspended while its journal remains in the notary's possession. What record obligation continues?
options: All records may be erased
Only future entries matter
The journal retention and location-notice duties
The journal must automatically become the employer's
questions.explanation: Section 1920(5) includes suspension among events requiring retention and notice of location.
feedback: Suspension does not authorize erasure.
Existing records remain subject to retention.

The employer is not the stated automatic recipient.

questions.stem: A journal's first entry is eleven years old but its final entry was last year. May the notary discard the whole volume now?
options: Yes, because the first entry is old
Yes, because a new volume is available
Only if a client agrees
No, count ten years from the last act chronicled
questions.explanation: The statutory retention anchor is the last act recorded in the journal.
feedback: The first entry does not start the whole-volume deadline.
Buying another journal does not shorten retention.
A client cannot waive the retention rule.

questions.stem: A required remote journal entry identifies the document but omits that the ceremony was an oath. What field needs correction?
options: The type of notarial act
The notary's age
The customer's shoe size
The provider's logo
questions.explanation: The entry must identify the notarial act type.
feedback: Correct. Record the actual oath/verification type.
The notary's age is not the missing transaction field.
Shoe size is unrelated.
A logo does not identify the act.

questions.stem: An office says that a video recording makes the remote journal unnecessary. Which statement follows Maine law?
options: One recording always replaces all written records
The remote act still requires a journal
Only free remote acts need journals
The employer chooses whether to comply
questions.explanation: Section 1920 separately requires a journal for all remote acts.
feedback: Recording and journal requirements are distinct.
Correct. Preserve both required records.
Fees do not determine journal scope.
Employer policy does not override the statute.

questions.stem: A notary's employer paid for a paper journal and asks to keep it when the notary leaves. What does the official course say?
options: Payment always transfers ownership
The customer owns the journal
The journal belongs to the notary
The vendor decides ownership
questions.explanation: The course states the journal belongs to the notary even if the employer paid.
feedback: The course expressly states otherwise.
A customer does not own the volume.
Correct. Preserve the notary's record responsibility.
Vendor preference does not control the official rule.

questions.stem: A notary performs in-person electronic work and keeps a permanent bound paper journal. Does §1920 categorically forbid a tangible journal format?
options: Yes, only cloud journals are allowed
Yes, every electronic act needs a spreadsheet
Yes, paper journals are never permitted
No, the statute permits tangible or electronic journal formats
questions.explanation: The statute permits both formats, subject to their integrity requirements.
feedback: The statute does not impose cloud-only storage.
A spreadsheet is not the sole authorized format.
Tangible journals are expressly permitted.
Correct. Format and compliance must be evaluated together.

questions.stem: A notary voluntarily journals an in-person paper acknowledgment. Which retention duty should be applied to that journal?
options: The ten-year period after the last act chronicled
No retention because paper journaling began voluntarily
Only one day
Only until the appointment ends
questions.explanation: Section 1920 requires retention of the officer's journal for ten years after its last act.
feedback: Correct. Voluntary maintenance does not justify immediate disposal.
The statute's retention language covers the journal.
One day does not satisfy the period.
Appointment completion does not end retention.

questions.stem: A notary uses two simultaneous paper journals for tangible acts and plans to merge them at renewal. What should be corrected?
options: Only the covers' colors
The one-active-journal tangible-record arrangement
Only the renewal payment
Only the customer receipts
questions.explanation: The one-journal-at-a-time requirement applies when chronicling tangible-record acts.
feedback: Color does not cure the arrangement.
Correct. Later merging does not remove the current statutory limit.
Payment does not resolve journal format.
Receipts are different records.

questions.stem: A required entry lists only a business's name even though an individual appeared. What statutory field must be captured?
options: Only the business's annual revenue
Only the recipient's address
The full name and address of each individual for whom the act is performed
Only the notary's office address
questions.explanation: The journal statute requires the individual's full name and address.
feedback: Revenue does not identify the appearing individual.
The recipient may be a different person.

The notary's address does not replace the individual's.

questions.stem: A former notary sends a journal to a storage company never approved by the Secretary and assumes §1920(6) is satisfied. What matters?
options: Only the company's low price
Only the company's logo
Only whether it advertises nationally
The repository must be approved by the Secretary
questions.explanation: The statutory alternative specifies the Secretary or an approved repository.
feedback: Price does not establish approval.
A logo does not establish approval.
Advertising reach does not establish approval.

questions.stem: A lost journal is recovered before renewal, and the notary wonders whether discovery of the earlier loss required reporting. What is the statutory trigger?
options: Discovery that the journal was lost or stolen
The next paid act
The journal's purchase anniversary
A client's lawsuit
questions.explanation: Section 1920(4) requires prompt notice on discovery of loss or theft.
feedback: Correct. The duty is tied to discovery.
A later act does not trigger the original notice.
Purchase anniversary is unrelated.

questions.stem: A Maine notary's spouse requests a notarization unrelated to money. What does §1904 provide?
options: The act is allowed if no fee is charged
The act is allowed if unrelated to property
The notary may not perform the act for the spouse
The employer can grant permission
questions.explanation: The family prohibition applies to performing an act for a spouse.
feedback: A fee waiver does not remove the relationship prohibition.
The prohibition is not confined to property records.

questions.stem: An unrelated signer appears on a record giving the notary's child a direct beneficial interest. What should happen?
options: Proceed because the signer is unrelated
Proceed if the child is absent
Proceed if the notary uses no stamp
Decline because the record creates the covered family interest
questions.explanation: The record-interest prohibition extends to the listed family members even if they are not the appearing signer.

Absence does not erase the beneficiary's interest.
Omitting a stamp does not remove the conflict.

questions.stem: A notary's half sibling needs an acknowledgment. Which statutory family category matters?
options: The expressly included half-relative category
Only blood siblings with two shared parents
Only relatives living in the same house
Only relatives under age 18

feedback: Correct. The relationship is included.
The statute expressly reaches half relatives.
Residence does not remove the prohibition.

questions.stem: A notary's parent is a party to an instrument signed by someone else. What conflict rule applies?
options: Only the appearing person's relationship counts
The listed family's party status in the record is independently disqualifying
A parent may waive every conflict

feedback: The statute also considers parties to the record.

A private waiver does not remove the prohibition.

questions.stem: A bank employee-notary is not a party to the bank's instrument and is asked to acknowledge another party. What does the corporate provision address?
options: All bank employment bars every act
A bank employee can notarize their own party signature
The statutory corporate authority may permit the described act subject to its limits
Banks require no identity checks
questions.explanation: Section 1904(4) permits specified corporate-associated acts while preserving party restrictions.
feedback: Corporate association is not an automatic bar to every listed act.
Party acknowledgment remains restricted.

Identity requirements continue.

questions.stem: A corporate officer-notary is individually a party to an instrument executed to the corporation. May the officer take its acknowledgment under the corporate provision?
options: Yes, corporate employment waives party status
Yes, if the corporation pays
Yes, if the instrument is short
No, the corporate provision preserves the party prohibition
questions.explanation: The corporate provision makes acknowledgment unlawful when the officer is a party individually or as corporate representative.
feedback: The exception preserves this restriction.
Payment does not remove party status.
Length does not determine the conflict.

questions.stem: A notary is paid to promote a direct initiative and is asked to administer its petition circulator's oath. What applies?
options: The nonnotarial promotion services create the statutory prohibition
Promotion never affects notarial work
