Correct. Complete the required record association.
A later call does not create the required electronic record.

questions.stem: A remote act is performed for a signer on paper. The officer assumes stamp use is optional because the source is paper. What does the FAQ say?
options: Every paper act is unstamped
Only a stamp vendor can decide
Only the customer's preference matters
A stamp is required for all remote notarizations
questions.explanation: The official FAQ requires stamp use for remote as well as electronic notarizations.
feedback: The remote category changes the guidance.
Vendor preference does not set the requirement.
The customer cannot waive the stated requirement.
Correct. Apply the remote requirement.

questions.stem: An electronic-record customer demands a technology the officer has not selected. What does §1921 provide?
options: The customer may not require use of an unselected technology
The customer can compel any software
Only the customer's employer chooses
A private invoice overrides selection
questions.explanation: The officer may select qualifying technologies and cannot be required to use an unselected one.
feedback: Correct. The statute protects the officer's technology choice.
The statute expressly limits that demand.
An employer does not replace the officer's statutory choice.
An invoice does not override the statute.

questions.stem: A notary selects an ordinary editable document tool for electronic acts without tamper evidence. Which statutory quality is required?
options: Only low cost
Tamper-evident technology
Only a popular brand
Only a large screen
questions.explanation: Section 1921(1) authorizes selection of tamper-evident technologies subject to approval requirements.
feedback: Low cost does not establish integrity.
Correct. Tamper evidence is a statutory characteristic.
Popularity does not establish compliance.
Screen size does not provide record integrity.

questions.stem: A notary sends an electronic notice but omits the intended technology. What does the statute require?
options: Only the customer's location
Only the notary's favorite color
Identification of the technology intended for use
Only the number of business cards
questions.explanation: Initial electronic notice must identify the intended technology, which is subject to state approval.
feedback: Customer location does not identify the technology.
Color is unrelated.
Correct. The intended technology must be disclosed.
Business cards are unrelated.

questions.stem: An accurate tangible copy of an electronic record with a notarial certificate is submitted for recording. What does §1921(3) permit?
options: Every clerk must accept every printout without review
The copy automatically proves title
No printout can ever qualify
A register of deeds may accept the officer-certified accurate copy under the stated original-record rule
questions.explanation: The statute uses may and conditions the provision on the officer's accurate-copy certification.
feedback: The statute does not mandate unconditional acceptance.
The provision does not adjudicate title.
The statute expressly permits this possibility.
Correct. Preserve both the conditions and discretionary wording.

questions.stem: A remote principal has a hearing impairment. How does the statutory communication definition address accessibility?
options: It includes qualifying technology facilitating communication when necessary and consistent with other law
It categorically excludes all impaired principals
It eliminates identity requirements
It allows any unrelated recording
questions.explanation: Section 1915(1)(A) expressly accommodates qualifying communication technology for vision, hearing or speech impairments.
feedback: Correct. Apply the accessible technology provision and other requirements.
The statute expressly includes an accommodation provision.
Identity requirements remain.
The communication still must support the lawful act.

questions.stem: A notary confuses the FAQ's in-person electronic procedure with remote notarization. What distinction does the FAQ make?
options: Electronic records never use signatures
In-person electronic uses an electronic record/signature with the signer present, while remote uses approved communication technology for a distant signer
Remote acts need no appearance
All electronic acts are paper acts
questions.explanation: The FAQ explains electronic format and remote location as distinct aspects of service.
feedback: Electronic notarization expressly uses an electronic signature.
Correct. Classify format and location accurately.
Remote technology supplies a lawful form of appearance.
Electronic records are a different format.

questions.stem: Before electronic/remote approval, the notice asks for a certification about Maine law. What is required?
options: A promise never to read updates
Only an employer's opinion
The officer's certification of reading and understanding chapter39 and the administrative rules
Only a vendor discount code
questions.explanation: The FAQ identifies the officer's law-and-rule reading certification as part of the notice.
feedback: The stated process requires reading and understanding.
The certification belongs to the officer.
Correct. Complete the specified legal-knowledge certification.
A discount code does not supply the certification.

cards.title: Eligibility connection
cards.front: Which Maine connection qualifies an applicant?
cards.rule: Be a Maine resident or have a place of employment or practice in Maine, and satisfy the other statutory qualifications.
cards.boundary: Minimum age is 18 and the applicant must read and write English.
cards.mixup: A vacation visit or borrowed address does not establish the statutory connection.

cards.title: First-commission examination
cards.front: Who faces the statutory examination requirement?
cards.rule: An applicant without a current Maine commission must pass the Secretary-administered or approved examination based on the official course.
cards.boundary: The verified materials do not establish a current first-exam question count, clock or passing percentage.
cards.mixup: A practice-bank score is not the state's required examination result.

cards.title: Study coverage
cards.front: What subjects does the official course address?
cards.rule: The course covers laws, rules, procedures and ethics relevant to notarial acts.
cards.boundary: No fixed classroom attendance hours were verified.
cards.mixup: Reading a vendor catalog does not replace the official subject coverage.

cards.title: Two qualification deadlines
cards.front: Which post-appointment deadlines must be tracked?
cards.rule: Take the Dedimus Justice oath within 30 calendar days and return the completed qualification certificate within 45 calendar days of appointment.
cards.boundary: The oath and certificate return are separate steps.
cards.mixup: Timely oath-taking does not by itself return the certificate.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q5

cards.title: Affirming the office oath
cards.front: What alternative does a conscientious applicant have?
cards.rule: Section 1922 permits its specified affirmation substitutions for the appointment oath.
cards.boundary: The solemn qualification procedure before a Dedimus Justice remains required.
cards.mixup: Affirmation changes the pledge wording, not the need to qualify.

cards.title: Renewal finish line
cards.front: What remains after online renewal payment?
cards.rule: Print the required documents, appear before a Dedimus Justice and return the originally signed exam and oath as instructed.
cards.boundary: The service is available from 45 days before expiration through 90 days after expiration.
cards.mixup: Payment alone does not finish qualification or authorize expired acts.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State application and renewal instructions — Renewal instructions

cards.title: Profile changes
cards.front: When should commission information be updated?
cards.rule: Notify the Secretary within 30 calendar days of a change in submitted information. A name change also requires the Change of Signature form.
cards.boundary: The official profile service has no update fee.
cards.mixup: Updating an employer's records does not update the state commission.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q22

cards.title: Separate marriage office
cards.front: What authority supports wedding solemnization after 2023?
cards.rule: Maine created a separate Marriage Officiant office and repealed the notary commission's own marriage authority effective July 1, 2023.
cards.boundary: Verify the separate license and its requirements.
cards.mixup: An active notary commission alone does not establish current marriage authority.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q6

cards.title: Personal knowledge standard
cards.front: What makes an acquaintance legally useful for identity?
cards.rule: Sufficient dealings must provide reasonable certainty that the appearing person has the identity claimed.
cards.boundary: Recognition of a name or public photograph alone does not establish those dealings.
cards.mixup: Another person's acquaintance is not automatically the officer's personal knowledge.

cards.title: Government identity categories
cards.front: How does Maine describe documentary evidence?
cards.rule: The statute lists passport, driver's license or government nondriver card and an alternative government-ID category containing signature or photograph satisfactory to the officer.
cards.boundary: Additional information may be required to assure identity.
cards.mixup: Do not import another state's photo-and-signature rule into the alternative Maine category.

cards.title: Credible witness foundation
cards.front: Which evidence supports a credible witness's participation?
cards.rule: The witness personally appears, gives oath/affirmation verification and is known to the officer or identified by the listed credentials.
cards.boundary: A credible witness actually vouches for the individual's identity.
cards.mixup: An unsworn introduction is not this statutory method.

cards.title: Physical inability procedure
cards.front: How is a directed signature documented?
cards.rule: A disabled person physically unable to sign may direct someone other than the officer to sign. Insert the statutory or similar direction statement.
cards.boundary: The actual act's appearance and identity requirements still matter.
cards.mixup: The notary is excluded as the directed signer under§1909.

cards.title: Capacity and free choice
cards.front: When can uncertainty about the signer support refusal?
cards.rule: The officer may refuse if not satisfied that the signer has competence/capacity or that the signature is knowingly and voluntarily made.
cards.boundary: General refusal is subject to other laws that prohibit refusal.
cards.mixup: A current credential answers identity, not every capacity or coercion concern.

cards.title: Prior execution versus sworn signing
cards.front: How do the course's signing procedures differ?
cards.rule: An acknowledgment may cover a prior signature after appearance and declaration. Verification and signature witnessing require signing before the officer under the course.
cards.boundary: An already signed verification/witnessing record must be signed again under those course steps.
cards.mixup: The certificate must describe the event actually performed.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slides20–27

cards.title: Certificate selection
cards.front: Who selects a missing certificate's act?
cards.rule: The signer decides which certificate to affix. The notary may provide examples or the signer may consult the recipient.
cards.boundary: Every act still needs the proper certificate.
cards.mixup: A short convenient form should not silently determine the customer's legal act.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q20–21

cards.title: Complete certificate facts
cards.front: Which details must a Maine notary certificate show?
cards.rule: Include actual date, jurisdiction, office title, filed-manner signature, legible printed/typed name and commission expiration.
cards.boundary: Execute the certificate only after performing the act and connect it to the record.
cards.mixup: A stamp alone does not supply every certificate requirement.

cards.title: Copy determination
cards.front: What exactly does the copy act certify?
cards.rule: The officer determines that the copy is a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction of the source record or item.
cards.boundary: The certification concerns the reproduction's accuracy.
cards.mixup: It does not guarantee the source's authenticity, contents or legal effects.
cards.source: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 4 §1905 — §1905(4); Course slide29

cards.title: Record-category screen
cards.front: Which records are excluded by the course?
cards.rule: Do not make notarial certified copies of vital or public records, including publicly recorded records available from their official source.
cards.boundary: A facial statement that copying is illegal is a separate restriction.
cards.mixup: A perfectly reproduced excluded record is still outside the described copy authority.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slides17,29–30

cards.title: Original comparison
cards.front: What supports a comparison certificate?
cards.rule: Carefully compare the copy with the original actually presented and determine that it is exact, complete and unaltered.
cards.boundary: Use certificate wording that truthfully describes the method used.
cards.mixup: A second photocopy does not supply an original for a claimed original comparison.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slides29–31

cards.title: Custodian participation
cards.front: How does the copy procedure begin?
cards.rule: Identify the record custodian if not personally known and determine that the presented source is an eligible original.
cards.boundary: Then make or witness the copy, or use the course's careful comparison method.
cards.mixup: A source's title alone does not establish custodian identity or eligibility.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slides30–31

cards.title: Complete reproduction
cards.front: What omissions defeat a full-copy statement?
cards.rule: Missing pages, cropped terms, unreadable source content and omitted reverse-side provisions prevent a full accurate reproduction.
cards.boundary: The certificate's stated scope must be truthful.
cards.mixup: A signature-page match does not establish a complete multipage copy.

cards.title: Secure copy certificate
cards.front: How is the certificate kept with the reproduction?
cards.rule: The course directs completing and signing the certificate and securely attaching it to the photocopy with a staple that would show removal.
cards.boundary: The statutory certificate must be part of or securely attached to the tangible record.
cards.mixup: An oral assurance or loose reusable certificate does not document the completed copy act.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slide30

cards.title: Electronic source to paper
cards.front: What authority covers printing an electronic record accurately?
cards.rule: Section 1904(2) permits certification of an accurate tangible copy of an electronic record.
cards.boundary: Section 1921(3) provides a conditioned may-accept recording provision for a register of deeds.
cards.mixup: The printout does not automatically establish title or unconditional acceptance.

cards.title: Authentication after copying
cards.front: Who certifies the notary's public authority for foreign use?
cards.rule: The Secretary issues apostilles or authentications as described in the official course.
cards.boundary: The receiving country's applicable process determines the authority certification.
cards.mixup: The notary's own copy stamp does not issue an apostille.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slide38

cards.title: Scope of mandatory recording
cards.front: Which Maine acts always require a journal?
cards.rule: All electronic and remote notarizations require journals. Traditional in-person paper journals are permitted and strongly recommended.
cards.boundary: A remote paper act is still remote.
cards.mixup: Paper record format alone does not remove a remote journal duty.

cards.title: Active journal arrangement
cards.front: How many simultaneous journals may be kept?
cards.rule: The statute allows one at a time for tangible-record acts and one or more for electronic-record acts.
cards.boundary: The record-format distinction remains relevant when arranging the records.
cards.mixup: Office count does not authorize multiple active tangible-record journals.

cards.title: Integrity of the medium
cards.front: What makes the journal format compliant?
cards.rule: Tangible journals are permanent bound registers with numbered pages. Electronic journals are permanent and tamper-evident.
cards.boundary: Electronic formats must comply with Secretary rules.
cards.mixup: Loose pages and silently editable notes lack the specified integrity.

cards.title: Entry timing and core fields
cards.front: When and what is recorded?
cards.rule: Make entries contemporaneously, including date/time, record description and act type, full individual name/address, identity basis and fee if any.
cards.boundary: Required recordkeeping follows the actual act.
cards.mixup: A later monthly reconstruction omits the contemporaneous requirement.

cards.title: Identity detail
cards.front: How is the identification basis preserved?
cards.rule: State personal knowledge when used. For satisfactory evidence, briefly describe the method and credential with issuance and expiration dates.
cards.boundary: Record what actually supported identity.
cards.mixup: A generic word such as identified may omit the specified detail.

cards.title: Ten-year anchor
cards.front: Which event starts journal retention?
cards.rule: Retain the journal for ten years after the last act chronicled in that journal.
cards.boundary: The first entry, purchase date and retirement date do not replace that anchor.
cards.mixup: An old first page does not make a recently used volume disposable.

cards.title: Loss and office exit
cards.front: What duties follow loss or cessation?
cards.rule: Promptly notify the Secretary of a lost or stolen journal. On resignation, revocation or suspension, retain it and report its location.
cards.boundary: The statute permits transfer to the Secretary or an approved repository instead.
cards.mixup: Leaving employment does not authorize discarding the official record.

cards.title: Death and known possession
cards.front: Who handles the journal after death or incompetency?
cards.rule: The representative, guardian or other knowing possessor transmits it to the Secretary or an approved repository.
cards.boundary: The statutory disposition duty applies to the responsible possessor.
cards.mixup: The journal does not become an ordinary box of disposable household papers.

cards.title: Payment and ownership
cards.front: Does an employer's purchase transfer the journal?
cards.rule: The official course states the commission, stamp and journal belong to the notary even when the employer pays.
cards.boundary: Record retention obligations continue independently of employment.
cards.mixup: A supply reimbursement does not make the commission shared office property.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slide36

cards.title: Two family conflict checks
cards.front: How does Maine screen family involvement?
cards.rule: Do not act for listed relatives. Also check whether the officer or a listed relative is a party or has a direct beneficial interest in the record.
cards.boundary: The statute includes spouse, domestic partner, parent, sibling, child, in-law, step and half relatives.
cards.mixup: An unrelated appearing signer does not eliminate a covered beneficiary conflict.

cards.title: Corporate provision limits
cards.front: When does corporate association differ from party status?
cards.rule: Section 1904(4) permits specified corporate-associated acts but prohibits the described acknowledgment where the officer is a party individually or as representative.
cards.boundary: Apply all stated conditions and other act requirements.
cards.mixup: Bank employment is neither a universal disqualification nor a waiver of party restrictions.

cards.title: Initiative promotion conflict
cards.front: What additional campaign role can bar a circulator oath?
cards.rule: An officer providing nonnotarial services to initiate or promote a direct initiative or people's veto cannot administer that measure's circulator oath or affirmation.
cards.boundary: The remote-election exclusions are separate checks.
cards.mixup: Choosing affirmation does not avoid a provision covering both oath and affirmation.

cards.title: Legal service boundary
cards.front: Which services does the commission not authorize?
cards.rule: It does not authorize legal drafting/advice/practice, immigration expertise or representation, or compensation for the listed activities.
cards.boundary: Independent lawful professional qualifications are separate from the commission.
cards.mixup: A client waiver does not create legal-practice authority.

cards.title: Advertising statement
cards.front: How is the nonattorney limitation disclosed?
cards.rule: A covered nonattorney's service advertisement includes the required prominent statement in each language used, subject to the stated limited size fallback.
cards.boundary: False/deceptive advertising and restricted notario titles are separately prohibited.
cards.mixup: English-only advertising does not create a blanket exemption.

cards.title: Original record access
cards.front: What limit protects the customer's original?
cards.rule: Except as otherwise allowed by law, the notary may not withhold access to or possession of the original provided for service.
cards.boundary: The commission does not create an automatic fee-dispute lien.
cards.mixup: Keeping a journal does not transfer ownership of the customer's original.

cards.title: Advance fee agreement
cards.front: How must a proposed notarial fee be arranged?
cards.rule: Disclose the fee in writing and obtain the individual's agreement before performing the act.
cards.boundary: The course says Maine does not statutorily set ordinary notarial service fees.
cards.mixup: No stated ordinary ceiling does not remove disclosure and consent requirements.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slide33

cards.title: Stamp lifecycle
cards.front: What happens when stamp authority ends or the device is lost?
cards.rule: Keep the device secure and prevent others using it. Render it unusable on the listed cessation/expiration events. Promptly report loss or theft.
cards.boundary: A responsible possessor has disabling duties after death or incompetency.
cards.mixup: An employer's payment does not authorize substitute use.

cards.title: Guidance on dual roles
cards.front: How should a witness/notary dual-role request be evaluated?
cards.rule: The course reports an Attorney General general guideline that a notary should not also act as witness in the same transaction.
cards.boundary: Present it as the stated guideline and separately check mandatory act requirements.
cards.mixup: Do not describe a recommendation as an invented universal criminal prohibition.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study — Slide37

cards.title: Approval before service
cards.front: Which prerequisites support electronic or remote work?
cards.rule: Submit the notice, identify approved technology, complete provider training and receive Secretary approval before initial service.
cards.boundary: The notice includes the officer's law/rule certification and signature/stamp example.
cards.mixup: A regular commission or generic camera account alone does not complete approval.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q13–16

cards.title: Maine officer and abroad principal
cards.front: Which location conditions matter?
cards.rule: The officer stays physically in Maine. An abroad principal needs the statutory United States connection and the signing/statement must not be prohibited locally.
cards.boundary: A qualifying principal may be outside Maine.
cards.mixup: A Maine venue label cannot cure an officer's actual out-of-state location.

cards.title: Remote identity alternatives
cards.front: Which routes establish remote identity?
cards.rule: Use statutory personal knowledge, a qualifying appearing credible witness's oath/affirmation, or at least two different types of approved identity proofing.
cards.boundary: The officer must also reasonably confirm the same record.
cards.mixup: A file name or email address alone does not supply the required identity determination.

cards.title: Recording and certificate
cards.front: What persists beyond the live remote act?
cards.rule: Create the audiovisual recording, preserve it under the statutory at-least-ten-year default and indicate communication technology in the certificate.
cards.boundary: The statute allows qualifying repository retention and rule-based retention standards.
cards.mixup: A journal entry does not replace the audiovisual recording.

cards.title: Absent tangible declaration method
cards.front: How does the statutory paper declaration procedure connect the records?
cards.rule: The principal signs the record and attached/integrated declaration during recording, sends both within four days, and the officer completes the stated certificate after receipt.
cards.boundary: A compliant act is effective on the declaration-signing date. The statute preserves other qualifying same-record procedures.
cards.mixup: This defined method should not be reduced to emailing a signature page.

cards.title: Election-specific exclusions
cards.front: Which requests need an in-person lawful route?
cards.rule: The remote statute excludes the listed absentee-ballot, candidate-oath, candidate-circulator, initiative-application and initiative-circulator acts.
cards.boundary: Remote marriage solemnization is also expressly prohibited.
cards.mixup: Clearing a promotional conflict does not remove a separate remote-act exclusion.

cards.title: Technology choice and updates
cards.front: What control does the officer keep over technology?
cards.rule: The officer selects qualifying tamper-evident technology and cannot be compelled to use an unselected system. Report provider changes within ten business days.
cards.boundary: State approval standards still apply.
cards.mixup: Customer preference does not convert an unapproved app into lawful technology.
cards.source: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 4 §1921 — §1921(1)-(2); FAQ Q17

cards.title: Electronic presence distinction
cards.front: How do format and physical distance differ?
cards.rule: The FAQ's in-person electronic procedure uses electronic records/signatures with the signer present. Remote work uses approved simultaneous sight-and-sound communication.
cards.boundary: The official guidance requires stamps and journals for electronic and remote acts.
cards.mixup: An electronic record is not automatically a remote transaction.
cards.source: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs — Q10–14,Q23

commission.summary: Maine qualification combines statutory eligibility, the required examination, appointment and a Dedimus Justice oath. Renewal has its own online and original-document steps.

sections.heading: Establish eligibility and examination completion
sections.body: Applicants are at least 18, can read and write English and have Maine residence or a place of employment or practice in Maine. They must meet the statutory disqualification and examination requirements. Section 1923 requires the examination for an applicant without a current Maine commission and provides a course covering laws, rules, procedures and ethics. Current first-examination count, duration and percentage were not verified.

sections.heading: Finish appointment and track renewal
sections.body: Use the most recent first-application form and deliver it with the required fee under the official instructions. After appointment, take the oath or authorized affirmation before a Dedimus Justice within 30 calendar days and return the qualification certificate within 45 calendar days. Terms last seven years. Renewal uses Total Notary Solution from 45 days before through 90 days after expiration, with the required examination, printing, Dedimus oath and original-document return.

sections.heading: Keep the state record current
sections.body: Notify the Secretary within 30 calendar days of changes in submitted information, including the additional Change of Signature form for a name change. The official course places Maine acts within Maine and assigns the commission, stamp and journal to the notary even when an employer paid. Marriage officiating has been a separate office since July 1, 2023. An active notary commission alone does not establish that separate authority.

example.heading: Payment followed by qualification
example.body: An applicant pays the fee and receives a Certificate of Qualification. The applicant schedules the Dedimus oath within the 30-day limit and returns the completed certificate within 45 days. Paying or obtaining a stamp does not eliminate these steps. The applicant waits until the required qualification and commission process is complete before serving customers.

keyFacts: Minimum age is 18 with a Maine residence/work/practice connection.
The commission term is seven years.
Track the 30-day oath and 45-day certificate-return deadlines separately.
Online renewal payment is followed by printed original-document and oath steps.
Current first-exam count, clock and passing percentage remain unverified.

identification.summary: Identify the actual appearing person, assess voluntary participation and perform the ceremony recorded in the certificate.

sections.heading: Use the Maine identity methods
sections.body: Personal knowledge comes from dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty. The statutory documentary categories include passports, driver's licenses, government nondriver cards and other satisfactory government identification containing signature or photograph. A credible witness personally appears and gives sworn or affirmed verification, with the witness known to the officer or identified through the listed credentials. Additional information may be required to assure identity.

sections.heading: Match participation and ceremony
sections.body: The officer may refuse when not satisfied about competence/capacity or knowing voluntary signing, subject to other law. A physically disabled principal unable to sign may direct an individual other than the officer to sign, with the required notation. The official course permits acknowledgment of a prior signature after appearance and declaration. Verification and signature witnessing require signing before the officer, including signing again if already signed under those course procedures.

sections.heading: Execute the truthful certificate
sections.body: Every act has a certificate with actual date, jurisdiction, officer title, official signature, legible name and the notary public's commission expiration. A notary signs in the manner on file with the Secretary. The act precedes signing the certificate, and the certificate is securely attached or properly associated with its record. If the record lacks a certificate, the signer chooses the act with examples or recipient guidance as needed.

example.heading: A hesitant signer and companion
example.body: A customer presents a qualifying credential while a companion pressures the customer to sign. The credential supports identity, but it does not establish voluntary action. The notary separately evaluates knowing and voluntary signing and may refuse if unsatisfied. Any completed certificate must reflect the act actually performed.

keyFacts: The alternative government-ID category uses signature or photograph.
The witness method requires actual oath/affirmation verification.
An officer may ask for additional identity assurance.
Section 1909 excludes the officer as directed third-person signer.
A stamp alone does not replace the required certificate.

copy-certification.summary: Maine permits accurate-copy acts while excluding the public and vital records described in the official course. Accuracy and eligibility must both be established.

sections.heading: Screen the record and source
sections.body: The officer determines that a certified copy is full, true and accurate. The official course excludes public records, vital records and publicly recorded documents available as certified copies from an official source. It also excludes records stating on their face that copying is illegal. Identify the custodian if not personally known and inspect the eligible original before making, witnessing or carefully comparing the reproduction.

sections.heading: Document the limited accuracy determination
sections.body: The copy certificate describes the actual reproduction method. It does not guarantee the original record's authenticity, contents or legal effects. Missing pages, cropped terms, unreadable passages and omitted reverse-side content prevent a statement that the full record was accurately reproduced. Complete and sign the certificate and securely attach it to the copy. The course describes stapling that would show removal.

sections.heading: Handle electronic sources and foreign use distinctly
sections.body: Section 1904(2) permits certification of an accurate tangible copy of an electronic record. Section 1921(3) allows a register of deeds to accept a qualifying certified tangible copy under its stated original-record provision. Apostilles and authentications are separate Secretary-issued certifications of official authority described in the course. A notarial copy certificate does not itself issue an apostille.

example.heading: A private agreement with an omitted exhibit
example.body: A custodian presents an eligible original private agreement and a copy missing the exhibit. The notary cannot certify that incomplete copy as full and accurate. After the complete reproduction is prepared and checked, the notary uses truthful certificate wording describing the actual method and securely attaches it.

keyFacts: Certify a full, true and accurate reproduction.
Public/vital-record exclusions remain even when the copy is accurate.
Do not certify a record with the stated facial copying prohibition.
Copy certification does not guarantee source authenticity or legal effects.
A Secretary-issued apostille is a separate authority certification.

journals.summary: Electronic and remote acts require journals. Traditional in-person paper journaling is permitted and strongly recommended, with format and retention duties once maintained.

sections.heading: Apply scope and format by the actual act
sections.body: Section 1920 requires journals for all electronic and remote notarizations. The statute allows one active journal for tangible-record acts and one or more for electronic-record acts. A tangible journal is a permanent bound register with numbered pages. An electronic journal is permanent and tamper-evident under applicable rules. A remote act on paper still falls within the remote journal requirement.

sections.heading: Record the transaction as it occurs
sections.body: The contemporaneous entry includes date/time, record description and act type, full name/address, identity basis and fee if any. State when identity rests on personal knowledge. For satisfactory evidence, briefly describe the method and credential including issuance and expiration dates. A recording does not replace these journal duties, and a monthly reconstruction does not satisfy contemporaneous entry timing.

sections.heading: Retain and dispose under the statute
sections.body: Retain the journal ten years after its last chronicled act. Promptly report loss or theft to the Secretary. On resignation, revocation or suspension, retain it and inform the Secretary of location, or use the permitted transfer to the Secretary or approved repository. Following death or adjudicated incompetency, the responsible representative, guardian or knowing possessor has the specified transmission duty.

example.heading: Retiring with a recently used volume
example.body: A notary retires with a volume opened twelve years ago but last used this year. The last act controls the ten-year retention period. The notary reports the journal's location or uses the authorized transfer alternative, preserving the record independently of the end of employment.

keyFacts: All electronic and remote acts require a journal.
Tangible-record acts use one active journal at a time.
Record entries contemporaneously.
Retention runs ten years from the last act in the journal.
An approved repository can satisfy the statutory alternative disposition.

prohibited-acts.summary: Maine's conflict rules cover both the person served and the interests in the record. Advertising, service fees and original-document access have separate limits.

sections.heading: Screen family, corporate and petition relationships
sections.body: Do not act for the listed family members, including spouse/domestic partner, parent, sibling, child, in-law, step or half relatives. Also check whether the officer or a listed relative is a party or has a direct beneficial interest in the record. The corporate provision permits specified acts but preserves party restrictions. An officer providing nonnotarial promotion/initiation services for an initiative or people's veto cannot administer that measure's circulator oath or affirmation.

sections.heading: Describe and charge only lawful services
sections.body: The commission does not authorize legal drafting/advice/practice, immigration expertise or representation, or compensation for those listed activities. Covered nonattorney advertising carries the required prominent limitation statement in each language, with the stated limited size fallback. False/deceptive advertising and the restricted notario titles are prohibited. The course requires written disclosure of a proposed notarial fee and the individual's agreement before the act.

sections.heading: Protect original records and official tools
sections.body: Except as otherwise allowed by law, do not withhold the customer's original record. Keep the stamping device secure and prevent another person's use. Disable it on the statutory cessation/expiration events and promptly report loss or theft. The official course's advice against serving both as separate witness and notary in the same transaction is presented as the stated Attorney General general guideline.

example.heading: An unrelated signer with a family beneficiary
example.body: An unrelated customer brings a record giving the notary's child a direct beneficial interest. The notary checks the record as well as the appearing person's relationship. Because the listed family interest triggers the statute, a different authorized officer must perform the act. A no-fee offer does not remove the conflict.

keyFacts: Check both the person served and parties/beneficiaries in the record.
The listed relatives include in-laws and step/half relatives.
Initiative promotion and remote-election exclusions are separate rules.
Fee disclosure and agreement occur before the act.
The commission does not authorize withholding originals as a general collection device.

electronic-ron.summary: Maine requires notice, approved technology, provider training and state approval for electronic or remote service. The remote statute adds location, identity, recording and document controls.

sections.heading: Complete the approval and identity process
sections.body: Submit the notice identifying approved technology, provider training/user certification, legal-reading certification and signature/stamp example, then receive Secretary approval before service. No additional Secretary test is required under the FAQ. Remote officers are physically in Maine. Use personal knowledge, a qualifying credible witness or at least two different types of identity proofing. Abroad principals also need the statutory United States connection and no local prohibition of the signing/statement.

sections.heading: Preserve the same record and required recording
sections.body: The officer reasonably confirms the record is the same one signed or used for the statement and creates the audiovisual recording. The certificate indicates communication technology. The statute provides an at-least-ten-year recording default subject to authorized rules. It contains a specific tangible-record declaration method with signing during the recording, transmission within four days, certificate after receipt and the statutory declaration-date effectiveness.

sections.heading: Recognize exclusions and continuing obligations
sections.body: The statute excludes the listed absentee-ballot, candidate, candidate-circulator and initiative/people's-veto acts remotely, and expressly prohibits remote marriage solemnization. Electronic and remote acts require the stamp and journal described by official guidance. Report provider changes within ten business days. The officer selects qualifying tamper-evident technology and cannot be compelled to use a system not selected.

example.heading: A circulator asks for a camera appointment
example.body: A candidate-petition circulator requests the oath remotely. Even if the officer is in Maine, uses an approved provider and has no family or campaign conflict, the specific remote-election exclusion must be applied. A lawful in-person route is needed for the listed act.

keyFacts: Approval precedes electronic or remote work.
The officer remains physically in Maine.
The statute provides three remote identity alternatives.
The tangible declaration method has a four-day transmission requirement.
Election-specific remote exclusions require document-level screening.

articles.keyword: Maine notary family conflict record beneficiary
articles.intent: Screen the signer and the record
articles.title: Maine Family Conflicts Beyond the Appearing Signer
articles.description: Apply Maine's relationship and record-interest rules to everyday office transactions.
articles.h1: Screening Family Interests in Maine Notarizations
articles.lede: The person at the desk is only one part of Maine's conflict review. The record's parties and direct beneficiaries can independently prevent the act.

sections.heading: Check the person receiving the act
sections.body: Section 1904(3)(A) prohibits acts for the listed relatives, including a spouse, domestic partner, parent, sibling, child, in-law and step or half relative. Imagine an office assistant whose half sibling asks for an acknowledgment of an unrelated business document. The absence of a financial benefit to the notary does not erase the listed relationship. Charging no fee also does not change who receives the act. The officer should arrange for a different authorized notarial officer.

sections.heading: Read the parties and beneficiaries
sections.body: A second customer is unrelated to the notary but presents a record granting the notary's child a direct beneficial interest. Section 1904(3)(B) independently addresses the officer's and listed relatives' party status or direct beneficial interests. The child need not be physically present for that conflict to matter. The transaction should therefore be screened from its contents and participants instead of relying only on the surname or relationship of the person requesting service.

sections.heading: Preserve the corporate provision's boundaries
sections.body: Section 1904(4) allows specified acts by an officer associated with a bank or corporation. It also expressly preserves restrictions when that officer is a party individually or as the corporation's representative. A bank employee's routine acknowledgment of another person's instrument presents different facts from acknowledging an instrument to which the employee is a party. Corporate employment should be evaluated under the actual provision while the officer continues checking all other act requirements.

sections.heading: Use the statute's consequence language
sections.body: Section 1904(6) describes acts violating the specified family, corporate or petition-conflict provisions as voidable. That term should be used accurately when explaining the rule. It does not give the notary permission to proceed merely because a later challenge may be needed. The practical task is to identify and avoid the disqualifying conflict before the certificate is executed. A customer's waiver or an employer's deadline does not remove the statutory prohibition.

faqs.q: Does an unrelated signer eliminate every family conflict?
faqs.a: No. A listed relative's party status or direct beneficial interest in the record is independently relevant.

faqs.q: Are half relatives included?
faqs.a: Section 1904(3)(A) expressly includes step and half relatives.

articles.keyword: Maine notary initiative petition circulator oath
articles.intent: Separate campaign conflicts from remote exclusions
articles.title: Two Separate Screens for Maine Petition Oaths
articles.description: Distinguish promotion conflicts from the election-specific remote prohibitions.
articles.h1: Maine Petition Oaths Need Two Different Checks
articles.lede: A circulator's request can raise both a conflict question and a remote-eligibility question. Satisfying one screen does not settle the other.

sections.heading: Identify the measure and additional services
sections.body: Section 1904(5) bars the officer from administering an initiative or people's-veto circulator oath or affirmation when the officer also provides nonnotarial services to initiate or promote that same effort. Suppose a campaign organizer drafts promotional material and then offers to notarize the effort's circulator affidavits. The officer's additional campaign services are central to this prohibition. Calling the declaration an affirmation does not avoid a provision covering both forms.

sections.heading: Check the separate remote exclusions
sections.body: Section 1915(16) separately excludes the listed candidate, candidate-petition circulator, initiative-application and initiative/people's-veto circulator acts from remote performance. An officer with no promotional role can therefore still lack remote authority for a listed petition oath. Approved technology, personal knowledge of the signer and physical presence of the officer in Maine do not remove an express act-specific exclusion from the remote statute.

sections.heading: Perform the lawful in-person ceremony
sections.body: When a listed oath uses its lawful in-person procedure, the officer still identifies the person and actually administers the oath or affirmation required for the statement. The official course identifies omitting that verbal declaration as a common error. A preprinted statement that a person swore before the officer does not perform the ceremony itself. Certificate facts must follow what occurred, and a signature already on a verification is handled under the course's signing-again instruction.

sections.heading: Preserve the review limits
sections.body: Maine's validity provision preserves the Secretary's ability to reject candidate, initiative or referendum petitions for improper notarization. It also does not validate acts by someone lacking authority. These limitations make accurate screening consequential even where a general validity provision may protect some acts from other technical defects. The officer should apply the actual conflict, appearance and election-specific requirements before certifying a circulator's statement.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Does no promotional role automatically permit a remote circulator oath?
faqs.a: No. Section 1915(16) separately excludes the listed election acts remotely.

faqs.q: Can affirmation wording avoid the promotion conflict?
faqs.a: Section 1904(5) covers both oath and affirmation.

articles.keyword: Maine remote notarization tangible record declaration
articles.title: Connecting a Maine Remote Tangible Record
articles.description: Track the declaration, four-day transmission and certificate steps for the statutory method.
articles.h1: Following Maine's Remote Tangible Declaration Procedure
articles.lede: A paper instrument outside the officer's physical presence needs a reliable same-record procedure. Section 1915(5) supplies one carefully defined method.

sections.heading: Record the principal's execution
sections.body: Under the subsection 5 method, the remotely located individual signs both the record and a declaration during the audiovisual recording. The declaration is part of or securely attached to the record and identifies the connection between the instrument and the remote act. Consider a principal signing a private business instrument at home while the approved officer remains in Maine. The procedure should record the required execution of both components rather than only a final signature-page image.

sections.heading: Send both components on time
sections.body: The principal sends the record and declaration to the officer no later than four days after the act. This deadline belongs to the specified declaration procedure and should not be confused with another state's paper-remote transmission rules. Sending the declaration alone does not provide the entire record-declaration package. The officer's reasonable same-record confirmation remains a statutory requirement, so completeness matters alongside the timing of the shipment.

sections.heading: Complete the certificate after receipt
sections.body: After receiving the record and declaration, the officer executes the certificate containing the prescribed or substantially similar statement about witnessing the individual sign by communication technology. Subsection 6 treats a compliant act as contemporaneous and effective on the date the principal signed the declaration. This is a specific statutory sequence. A certificate issued before the officer has the required received papers would bypass the described receipt step.

sections.heading: Keep this method within its statutory scope
sections.body: Subsection 7 preserves another procedure that satisfies subsection 3(B)'s same-record requirement. The declaration method therefore should not be described as the only conceivable procedure. Any alternative still needs to satisfy the applicable law and approval standards. The officer also needs identity evidence, an audiovisual recording, the required journal and technology notation, and must check the excluded remote acts before using any remote paper workflow.

faqs.q: When are the record and declaration sent under this method?
faqs.a: No later than four days after the notarial act.

faqs.q: Which date makes a compliant subsection 5 act effective?
faqs.a: Subsection 6 identifies the date the principal signed the required declaration.

articles.keyword: Maine notary credible witness directed signature
articles.intent: Keep identity and signing assistance distinct
articles.title: Identity Witnesses and Directed Signers in Maine
articles.description: Understand how a sworn identity witness differs from a person signing at a disabled principal's direction.
articles.h1: Two Different Helping Roles at a Maine Appointment
articles.lede: A companion may help establish identity or may affix a directed signature. Each role needs its own statutory foundation.

sections.heading: Establish the credible witness's function
sections.body: Section 1907(2)(B) permits identity verification on oath or affirmation by a credible witness who personally appears. The witness is known to the officer or identified through the listed passport, driver's-license or government nondriver-card route. A friendly introduction does not itself provide that solemn verification. The companion must actually vouch for the individual's identity under the procedure, while the officer remains responsible for being satisfied of identity.

sections.heading: Use additional assurance when needed
sections.body: Personal knowledge under section 1907(1) comes from dealings sufficient to give reasonable certainty of identity. A witness's relationship to the principal does not automatically become the officer's personal knowledge. Section 1907(3) permits requiring additional information or credentials necessary to assure identity. If the available evidence leaves the officer uncertain, the officer should resolve that uncertainty through a lawful method before completing the requested act.

sections.heading: Document a directed third-person signature
sections.body: Section 1909 addresses a person physically unable to sign due to disability. The principal may direct an individual other than the notarial officer to sign the principal's name. The officer inserts the statutory or similar statement identifying who affixed the signature and at whose direction. This is an execution procedure, not a substitute for identifying the principal or performing the actual acknowledgment, verification or other requested notarial act.

sections.heading: Assess participation separately from credentials
sections.body: A credential or witness can support identity while leaving a capacity or coercion concern unresolved. Section 1908 permits refusal when the officer is not satisfied that the individual has competence or capacity or that the signature is knowingly and voluntarily made. A companion's insistence cannot settle that judgment. The appointment should preserve the principal's own lawful participation, with a certificate accurately recording the act and any required directed-signature statement.

faqs.q: Must a credible witness always be personally known to the officer?
faqs.a: Maine also permits identification of the appearing witness through the specified credentials.

faqs.q: Can the notarial officer be the directed signer under section 1909?
faqs.a: The statute specifies an individual other than the notarial officer.

articles.keyword: Maine notary copy certification public vital records
articles.title: Maine Copy Certification Starts with the Record
articles.description: Distinguish eligible private sources from public, vital and facially restricted records.
articles.lede: A perfect photocopy can still be outside the authority described in Maine's official course. Identify the source category before certifying its reproduction.

sections.heading: Check the source category
sections.body: The official course excludes certified or attested notarial copies of public records and vital records. It also identifies publicly recorded documents available as certified copies from an official source and records stating on their face that copying is illegal. A customer bringing a birth certificate needs the authorized vital-record source. The notary's accurate copier and willingness to waive a fee do not change the source's legal category.

sections.heading: Verify the eligible original and custodian
sections.body: For an eligible private record, the course starts with identifying the custodian if not personally known and observing that the presented source is an original. The officer may make or witness the photocopy, and the course also provides a carefully compared-copy certificate. A claim that a copy was compared with the original must be based on the original actually presented. The certificate should describe the procedure the officer performed.

sections.heading: Review the complete reproduction
sections.body: Section 1905(4) requires a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction. A six-page private agreement missing its exhibit, a cropped handwritten term or an unreadable scanned paragraph cannot support the statement that the complete record was accurately reproduced. The officer should inspect the whole scope covered by the certificate. A matching title or signature page alone does not establish that every part of a multipage source was copied.

sections.heading: State the limited conclusion truthfully
sections.body: The official course explains that copy certification does not guarantee the original's authenticity, contents or effects. It also distinguishes this act from taking an oath or acknowledgment. The officer completes the appropriate certificate and securely attaches it to the photocopy, with the course describing a staple that leaves evidence of removal. Accurate wording and attachment preserve the limited reproduction determination without promising legal outcomes beyond the act.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Can a notary certify a vital-record copy because it is exact?
faqs.a: The official course excludes notarial certified copies of vital records.

faqs.q: Does copy certification prove the original's statements are true?
faqs.a: The course limits the act to copy accuracy and does not guarantee contents or effects.

articles.keyword: Maine electronic record tangible copy register deeds
articles.title: From an Electronic Maine Record to a Tangible Copy
articles.description: Study accurate-copy certification and the register of deeds' conditioned acceptance provision.
articles.h1: Paper Copies of Electronic Maine Records
articles.lede: Maine expressly addresses accurate tangible copies of electronic records. The officer's certification and the recording office's acceptance have different roles.

sections.heading: Use the express accurate-copy authority
sections.body: Section 1904(2) permits a notarial officer to certify that a tangible copy of an electronic record accurately copies that record. Suppose a business needs a paper reproduction of a completed electronic instrument. The officer compares the actual electronic source with the tangible output and determines accuracy. A printout missing a table or signature-related page cannot be treated as an accurate copy merely because its opening title matches.

sections.heading: Preserve the notarial certificate
sections.body: Section 1916(6) requires the certificate to be part of or securely attached to a tangible record and properly affixed or logically associated with an electronic record. The certificate itself includes the required officer identity, date, jurisdiction and other applicable fields. The paper reproduction and its certificate should therefore preserve their connection. A detached statement available for attachment to any later printout would not establish the specific record being certified.

sections.heading: Read may-accept precisely
sections.body: Section 1921(3) allows a register of deeds to accept a tangible copy of an electronic record containing a notarial certificate as meeting an original-record requirement when the executing officer certifies the copy's accuracy. The statute uses may and supplies conditions. It should not be rewritten as unconditional mandatory acceptance of every printout. A recording-office decision also does not turn the copy certificate into a guarantee of ownership or the transaction's substantive validity.

sections.heading: Keep authority certification separate
sections.body: If the record will be used abroad, the course describes apostille or authentication as a Secretary-issued certification of the notary's or public officer's authority. That is distinct from certifying the printout's accuracy. The notary's own seal does not issue an apostille, and neither process is a general promise that the underlying business terms will be enforced. The requester should identify the actual required record and authority certifications for the intended use.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Does section 1921 require every register to accept every printout?
faqs.a: It says a register may accept the stated qualifying accurately certified tangible copy.

faqs.q: Does a copy certificate issue an apostille?
faqs.a: No. The official course describes apostilles as Secretary-issued authority certifications.

articles.title: A Maine Journal's Life After Retirement
articles.description: Track the last-entry retention date, location notice and permitted repository transfer.
articles.h1: Retaining Maine Journals After Office Ends
articles.lede: Leaving the office does not end the journal's statutory life. The final recorded act supplies a separate retention anchor.

sections.heading: Find the actual last act
sections.body: Section 1920 requires ten years of retention after the performance of the last act chronicled in the journal. Imagine a volume opened twelve years ago and used until this spring. Its oldest entry does not make the whole volume ready for disposal. The notary identifies the final act date and preserves the volume through the statutory period. Buying a new book or ending employment does not replace that date.

sections.heading: Keep format and content usable
sections.body: A tangible journal is a permanent bound register with numbered pages, and an electronic journal is permanent and tamper-evident under applicable rules. Required entries are made contemporaneously and preserve the specified transaction and identification details. Retention should preserve the actual journal that records those acts. A stack of retyped summaries or a silently editable replacement file should not be assumed to provide the same statutory record.

sections.heading: Report location or use the authorized transfer
sections.body: On resignation, revocation or suspension, subsection 5 calls for retention under the normal period and notice to the Secretary of the journal's location. Subsection 6 permits transmission to the Secretary or a repository approved by the Secretary instead. An inexpensive storage company is not automatically an approved repository. The former officer should identify the statutory recipient or maintain the journal and supply the required location information.

sections.heading: Plan for loss and the responsible possessor
sections.body: Loss or theft triggers prompt notice to the Secretary on discovery. After death or adjudication of incompetency, the representative, guardian or other knowing possessor must transmit the journal to the Secretary or an approved repository. The course also states that the journal belongs to the notary even if an employer paid. These provisions support continuity beyond payroll status, office moves and the original officer's ability to handle the volume personally.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Does retirement start a new shorter retention period?
faqs.a: The statutory anchor remains ten years after the last act chronicled.

faqs.q: May any storage company serve as the statutory alternative repository?
faqs.a: Section 1920(6) specifies a repository approved by the Secretary.

articles.keyword: Maine notary fee written disclosure advertising
articles.title: Maine Service Fees, Advertising and Original Records
articles.description: Connect advance fee agreement with truthful advertising and protection of customer originals.
articles.h1: Customer-Facing Duties for a Maine Notary
articles.lede: The appointment begins before the certificate is signed. Fee agreement and advertising set expectations about the service the commission actually authorizes.

sections.heading: Agree to the fee before the act
sections.body: The official course states that Maine does not statutorily set ordinary notarial service fees. It requires any proposed notarial fee to be disclosed in writing and agreed to by the individual before the act. A business that first reveals the charge after notarization has missed that advance process. Written disclosure alone also leaves a step incomplete when the individual has not agreed before service.

sections.heading: Advertise the actual limited role
sections.body: Section 1926 says the commission does not authorize legal drafting, legal advice or practice, immigration expertise or representation, or compensation for those listed activities. Nonattorney notaries must avoid the restricted notario titles and false or deceptive advertising. An advertisement claiming the state guarantees the notary's legal advice would therefore misdescribe the role. A customer's willingness to pay does not expand the authority granted by the commission.

sections.heading: Supply the required limitation statement
sections.body: The covered nonattorney service advertisement includes the statutory or authorized limitation statement prominently in each language used. The statute reaches the stated oral and recorded representations, including broadcast, print and internet media. Its limited size fallback applies under the specified circumstances and requires prominent display or provision at the place before the act. An English-only advertisement should not be assumed exempt from the general Maine notice requirement.

sections.heading: Protect the customer's original
sections.body: Except as otherwise allowed by law, section 1926(5) prohibits withholding access to or possession of the original record provided for service. A fee dispute does not itself give the commission an automatic lien over the customer's document. The journal and any lawful service records serve their own purposes. The original remains subject to the statutory access protection, which should be respected even when the office is trying to collect an agreed charge.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Can the notary disclose the charge only after service?
faqs.a: The course requires written disclosure and the individual's agreement before the act.

faqs.q: Does a notary commission generally authorize keeping an original to collect a fee?
faqs.a: Section 1926(5) generally prohibits withholding the provided original except as otherwise allowed by law.

articles.keyword: Maine notarial certificate stamp optional paper
articles.intent: Keep certificate duties distinct from stamp guidance
articles.title: Maine Paper Certificates Need More Than a Stamp
articles.description: Read the mandatory certificate fields alongside optional ordinary-paper stamp guidance.
articles.lede: Optional stamp use for ordinary in-person paper work does not make the certificate optional. Each required field describes the act and officer.

sections.heading: Complete the mandatory certificate
sections.body: Section 1916 requires contemporaneous certificate execution, the officer's signature and date, jurisdiction, office title and legibly printed or typed name. A notary public also includes commission expiration and signs in the manner on file with the Secretary. A stamp-only mark on a document does not supply all these requirements. The officer should identify the act being certified and complete the statutory information from the actual appointment facts.

sections.heading: Use the actual act date and jurisdiction
sections.body: A contract can be drafted in Portland and acknowledged in another Maine county on a later day. The certificate describes the performed notarial act, so the preparation location and contract date do not automatically fill its venue and date. The statute also bars affixing or associating the officer's signature before the act has been performed. A customer's deadline does not authorize advance certification of a promised future appearance.

sections.heading: Connect the certificate to the specific record
sections.body: For a tangible record, the certificate must be part of or securely attached to the record. For an electronic record, it is affixed or logically associated under the applicable standards. If a document has no certificate, the FAQ says the signer chooses which act to request, with examples or recipient consultation available. The officer should avoid silently selecting a convenient legal act or issuing a loose certificate that can be reused on unrelated records.

sections.heading: Apply the stamp guidance to the right category
sections.body: The official course and FAQ make stamp use optional for ordinary in-person paper acts while strongly suggesting it unless prohibited. They require stamps for electronic and remote acts. A kept official stamp contains the specified commissioned name, Maine jurisdiction and expiration information and is reproducible with the record. The stamp's presence does not prove that appearance, identity or the verbal ceremony actually occurred, and it does not replace the officer's certificate.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs
Maine Secretary of State Notary Public Course of Study

faqs.q: Is the certificate optional when the paper stamp is optional?
faqs.a: No. Every notarial act must be evidenced by the required certificate.

faqs.q: Who chooses the act when a document lacks a certificate?
faqs.a: The FAQ assigns that decision to the signer, with examples or recipient guidance available.

articles.keyword: Maine electronic notarization versus remote appearance
articles.title: Electronic Records and Remote Presence in Maine
articles.description: Separate in-person electronic work from the approved remote communication procedure.
articles.h1: Two Dimensions of a Maine Electronic Appointment
articles.lede: An electronic signature describes format. A remotely located signer describes physical separation. Maine's official guidance addresses both.

sections.heading: Classify the appointment before selecting tools
sections.body: The FAQ describes in-person electronic notarization using an electronic record and signature while the signer is physically with the officer. It describes remote notarization using an approved technology provider for simultaneous sight-and-sound communication with a distant signer. A keypad used at the officer's desk does not itself make the transaction remote. A distant person's paper instrument can still create remote duties, including the journal and stamp requirements in the official guidance.

sections.heading: Finish the approval process first
sections.body: Before electronic or remote service, the officer submits the notice and receives Secretary approval. The FAQ identifies approved technology, provider training and approved-user certification, the officer's law/rule reading certification and signature/stamp example. It says no additional Secretary test is required for this approval, while provider technology training is required. A regular commission and personal familiarity with video apps do not complete that approval process.

sections.heading: Locate the officer and identify the principal
sections.body: For remote acts, the officer is physically in Maine and uses the authorized identity alternatives. An abroad principal also needs the statutory United States connection and no foreign prohibition of the signing or statement. The officer reasonably confirms the same record and creates the audiovisual recording. Technology cannot relocate an officer physically outside Maine, and a principal's Maine address does not cure the officer's actual out-of-state position.

sections.heading: Maintain the continuing technology duties
sections.body: Section 1921 permits selection of qualifying tamper-evident technologies and says another person cannot require a technology the officer has not selected. The FAQ requires provider-change notice within ten business days. The officer should therefore keep the state record aligned with the actual selected system and training. The remaining record, certificate and excluded-act rules continue to apply after the initial approval, including the election-specific remote prohibitions.

sources.title: Maine Secretary of State notary FAQs

faqs.q: Does an electronic signature automatically mean the signer is remote?
faqs.a: No. The FAQ describes an in-person electronic procedure as well as remote notarization.

faqs.q: Can an approved Maine officer perform the remote act while physically elsewhere?
faqs.a: The remote statute requires the officer to be located in Maine.
